"assets" for a //go:embed assets directive.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: RotateEvery
symbols.doc:
RotateEvery is how often kit makes a new version of a generated secret.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: Routine
symbols.doc:
Routine is a loop written by hand: a function that runs until its context
ends. kit starts it with the app, cancels its context on shutdown and waits
for it, restarts it after an error or a panic — backing off from one second
to one minute — and reads its select statements to draw what it waits on.

symbols.name: ScopeKey
symbols.doc:
ScopeKey is the name the scopes give in this process: 16 hex digits of the
SHA-256 of their values. A client computes the key the daemon computed
from the same declaration, and so finds its lock or its socket.

symbols.name: ScopeValue
symbols.doc:
ScopeValue is one part of a path computed at the start: the user, the
executable, a configuration directory. Two processes share a singleton or
a socket when every scope gives them the same value.

symbols.name: Secret
symbols.doc:
Secret is a secret the product declares: provided by the operator — an SMTP
URL, an API token — or generated by kit — a signing or sealing key — and
rotated on its schedule.

symbols.name: Open
symbols.doc:
Open decrypts a box any kept version sealed, with the aad it was sealed
with. A box no kept version opens — forged, altered, or sealed by a
version pruned since — is refused with an error errors.Is matches with
secret.SealInvalid.

symbols.name: Present
symbols.doc:
Present reports whether the secret is set now, where it lives: false, and
no error, when an [Optional] secret is given nowhere — which the product
answers by leaving off what needs it. An error says its store could not
be read. A secret the start required is present, unless the operator took
it back since.

	if ok, err := OpenAIKey.Present(ctx); err != nil || !ok {
		return Verdict{}, err // no key, no automatic screening
	}

symbols.name: Seal
symbols.doc:
Seal encrypts plaintext under the secret's current version, binding aad:
data that travels beside the box in the clear and must come back
unchanged for the box to open.

symbols.name: Sign
symbols.doc: Sign signs message with the secret's current version.

symbols.name: Value
symbols.doc:
Value returns the secret's current version. A provided secret is read
where it lives at every call.

symbols.name: Verify
symbols.doc:
Verify reports whether a kept version signed message: nil when one did,
and an error errors.Is matches with secret.SignatureInvalid when none did.

symbols.name: SecretConfigurer
symbols.doc: SecretConfigurer configures a secret.

symbols.name: SecretStore
symbols.doc:
SecretStore keeps the secrets in store instead of the environment's: a
test gives a store holding what its provided secrets hold. The
environment's variables are still read first.

symbols.name: Service
Activity
symbols.doc:
Activity declares that the service is busy while fn returns true: a daemon
whose clients are sessions, not connections, stops once the last session
ended rather than once the last connection closed. fn is called on the
idle watch's tick, from one goroutine, and must answer quickly; a panic
counts as busy, and is logged. The value is kept for the declaration:

	var _ = Service.Activity(func(context.Context) bool { return sessions.Open() > 0 })

symbols.name: AuthHandler
symbols.spelled: func[P, D any](name string, handler func(context.Context, P) (UID, D, error)) *AuthenticatorHandler[P, D]
symbols.canonical: func[P, D any](name string, handler func(context.Context, P) (github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.UID, D, error)) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.AuthenticatorHandler[P, D]
symbols.doc:
AuthHandler declares the app's authentication handler. The handler returns
the user's ID and data; an empty UID with a nil error means "no
credentials", which [Auth] endpoints answer 401 and [AuthOptional]
endpoints serve anonymously; an error — usually [Unauthenticated] — refuses
the request.

The handler runs only for a request that carries at least one of the
credentials' cookies or headers; a request with none is anonymous without
asking it.

symbols.name: CLI
symbols.spelled: func(name string, doc string, fn CLIFunc, opts ...CommandLineConfigurer) *CLI
symbols.canonical: func(name string, doc string, fn github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.CLIFunc, opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.CommandLineConfigurer) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.CLI
symbols.doc:
CLI declares a command named name, which Main runs when the process is
called "<binary> <name> ...". doc is its one-line help.

symbols.name: Command
symbols.spelled: func[C, R any](name string, handler func(context.Context, C) (R, error), opts ...CommandConfigurer) *Command[C, R]
symbols.canonical: func[C, R any](name string, handler func(context.Context, C) (R, error), opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.CommandConfigurer) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.Command[C, R]
symbols.doc:
Command declares a command of the service: an operation named name, run by
handler, that changes something. Its node is "<service>/command/<name>".

	var PlaceOrder = Service.Command("place-order", placeOrder).
		Allow(Policy, "place", "order").
		Expose("POST /orders")

symbols.name: Cron
symbols.spelled: func(name string, expr string, fn func(context.Context) error) *Job
symbols.canonical: func(name string, expr string, fn func(context.Context) error) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.Job
symbols.doc:
Cron declares a job that runs on a five-field POSIX cron expression, in the
process's local time zone.

symbols.name: Endpoint
symbols.spelled: func[Req, Resp any](route string, handler func(context.Context, Req) (Resp, error), opts ...EndpointConfigurer) *EndpointService[Req, Resp]
symbols.canonical: func[Req, Resp any](route string, handler func(context.Context, Req) (Resp, error), opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.EndpointConfigurer) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.EndpointService[Req, Resp]
symbols.doc:
Endpoint declares an HTTP endpoint on route — "METHOD /path/{param}" — run
by handler. The request is decoded from the path, the query, the headers
(fields tagged `path:"…"`, `query:"…"`, `header:"…"`) and the JSON body
(every other field), then checked against its `validate` tags, then handed
to the policies ([RateLimit], [Timeout], [Bulkhead]) and the handler. The
response is JSON, or 204 No Content when it is [EmptyValue].

An endpoint is for what HTTP itself is about — a webhook a third party
calls. A business operation is a command or a query, exposed on its route
([Command.Expose], [Query.Expose]), and run in process by the code that
needs it ([Command.Dispatch], [Query.Ask]).

The endpoint's name, and so its node ID, is the handler's function name.

symbols.name: Every
symbols.spelled: func(name string, period time.Duration, fn func(context.Context) error) *Job
symbols.canonical: func(name string, period time.Duration, fn func(context.Context) error) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.Job
symbols.doc:
Every declares a job that runs every period, first one period after the
app starts.

symbols.name: Go
symbols.doc:
Go declares a hand-written loop. run must return when ctx ends; returning
earlier, with or without an error, restarts it after a backoff.

Everything run does is drawn from the loop's node: a store it reads, a
topic it publishes on. kit has no span around it — a run lasts as long as
the app — so each of those calls starts a trace of its own.

symbols.name: Implement
symbols.spelled: func[Req, Resp any](port *PortService[Req, Resp], handler func(context.Context, Req) (Resp, error), opts ...EndpointConfigurer) *EndpointService[Req, Resp]
symbols.canonical: func[Req, Resp any](port *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.PortService[Req, Resp], handler func(context.Context, Req) (Resp, error), opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.EndpointConfigurer) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.EndpointService[Req, Resp]
symbols.doc:
Implement declares that the service implements port: an endpoint of the
service with no route, which only the port reaches, in process, when the
app binds nothing else and this is the one implementation among the
services it mounts. It runs as every endpoint does — the request's
validate tags, the options' policies, the caller's user — and is named
like one: its [Name], else its handler's name, else, for a function
literal, the port's name. A handler whose request or response is not the
port's does not compile. A host implements a module's port on its own
service: it never adds a node to the module's.

	var _ = posts.Service.Implement(desk.Enforcer, Enforce)

symbols.name: Listen
symbols.spelled: func(name string, contract string, handler ListenHandler, opts ...ListenerConfigurer) *Listener
symbols.canonical: func(name string, contract string, handler github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.ListenHandler, opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.ListenerConfigurer) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.Listener
symbols.doc:
Listen declares a listener named name speaking contract — "<name>/v<major>",
"render/v1" — whose connections handler serves, one goroutine each.

symbols.name: Loop
symbols.spelled: func(name string, run func(context.Context, WakeEvent) error, opts ...LoopConfigurer) *Loop
symbols.canonical: func(name string, run func(context.Context, github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.WakeEvent) error, opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.LoopConfigurer) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.Loop
symbols.doc:
Loop declares a loop run by kit: run is called once at start, then on
every wake.

Runs never overlap: wakes that come while the function runs are gathered
into one run after it. A run that fails or panics is counted, and the next
one waits a backoff — one second, doubling up to a minute — unless it is
a [Loop.Nudge]. A deadline already past wakes the loop at once, but never
sooner than a second after the previous run: a WakeAt that keeps answering
the past costs a run a second, not a spinning core.

symbols.name: Mailer
symbols.doc: Mailer declares outbound mail.

symbols.name: Name
symbols.doc:
Name returns the service name, which is also its node ID: qualified with
its module's, "moderation.intake", when a module lists it.

symbols.name: Port
symbols.spelled: func[Req, Resp any](name string, opts ...PortConfigurer[Req, Resp]) *PortService[Req, Resp]
symbols.canonical: func[Req, Resp any](name string, opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.PortConfigurer[Req, Resp]) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.PortService[Req, Resp]
symbols.doc:
Port declares a port of the service: an operation it needs, named name,
taking Req and answering Resp, which another service implements
([Service.Implement]) or the app binds ([Bind]). Its node is
"<service>/port/<name>"; its doc is its declaration's doc comment.

symbols.name: Query
symbols.spelled: func[Q, R any](name string, handler func(context.Context, Q) (R, error), opts ...QueryConfigurer) *Query[Q, R]
symbols.canonical: func[Q, R any](name string, handler func(context.Context, Q) (R, error), opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.QueryConfigurer) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.Query[Q, R]
symbols.doc:
Query declares a query of the service: an operation named name, run by
handler, that reads and changes nothing. Its node is
"<service>/query/<name>".

	var MyOrders = Service.Query("my-orders", myOrders, kit.Auth()).Expose("GET /orders", kit.AnyUser())

symbols.name: Secret
symbols.doc:
Secret declares a secret the product needs.

Without an option it is provided: the operator gives it in the
environment — the variable <APP>_<NAME>, TODO_STRIPE_KEY for the secret
"stripe-key" of the app "todo", or TODO_STRIPE_KEY_FILE naming a file that
holds it, the Docker and Kubernetes way — or in the environment's store,
with `kit secrets set`. It is read at every use, so replacing it where it
lives takes effect without a restart, and a start without it fails, naming
the variable to set.

With [Optional], a start without it goes on: the product asks
[Secret.Present] before it uses the secret.

With [Generated], kit makes it: version 1 on the first start, a new version
on its schedule, the previous ones kept so that what they sealed or signed
still opens and verifies. It lives in the store the environment keeps — an
encrypted file store in dev, KIT_SECRETS elsewhere. Its variable pins it:
kit then uses the value as it is and does not rotate it.

name is 1 to 63 lower-case letters, digits and dashes, starting and ending
with a letter or a digit — one grammar for a file name and a variable — and
unique in the app.

symbols.name: Setting
symbols.spelled: func[T SettingValue](name string, def T, opts ...SettingConfigurer) *SettingService[T]
symbols.doc:
Setting declares a setting of the service: name holds def unless the
environment says otherwise — the variable <APP>_<NAME>, TODO_BASE_URL for
the setting "base-url" of the app "todo", or the key name in the product's
configuration files. [SettingService.Get] reads it.

name follows the secrets' grammar — 1 to 63 lower-case letters, digits and
dashes, starting and ending with a letter or a digit — and is unique in the
app, among its settings and its secrets: the two share their variables.

symbols.name: Static
symbols.spelled: func(name string, prefix string, fsys fs.FS, opts ...StaticConfigurer) *Frontend
symbols.canonical: func(name string, prefix string, fsys io/fs.FS, opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.StaticConfigurer) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.Frontend
symbols.doc:
Static declares a frontend serving fsys under prefix, which must end with
'/'. A path with no file extension that matches no file serves index.html,
so client-side routing works; a missing file with an extension — a script,
a stylesheet — stays a 404. A directory is never listed. The SDK's static
handler serves it; kit draws it and observes every request.

symbols.name: Store
symbols.spelled: func[T any](name string, key func(T) string, opts ...StoreConfigurer) *StoreService[T]
symbols.canonical: func[T any](name string, key func(T) string, opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.StoreConfigurer) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.StoreService[T]
symbols.doc: Store declares a store of entities of type T, keyed by key.

symbols.name: Subscribe
symbols.spelled: func[T any](name string, topic *TopicService[T], handler func(context.Context, T) error, opts ...SubscriptionConfigurer) *SubscriptionWorker[T]
symbols.canonical: func[T any](name string, topic *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.TopicService[T], handler func(context.Context, T) error, opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.SubscriptionConfigurer) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.SubscriptionWorker[T]
symbols.doc:
Subscribe declares a subscription of the service to topic. Delivery is at
least once: handler must be idempotent, which is the one thing the SDK's
queue cannot check and kit therefore asks you to promise here.

symbols.name: Topic
symbols.doc: Topic declares a topic carrying messages of type T.

symbols.name: Watch
symbols.spelled: func(name string, mark Mark, handler func(context.Context, WrittenEvent) error, opts ...SubscriptionConfigurer) *Watch
symbols.canonical: func(name string, mark github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.Mark, handler func(context.Context, github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.WrittenEvent) error, opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.SubscriptionConfigurer) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.Watch
symbols.doc:
Watch declares a watch of the service: handler is told of every write kit
confirms on a store whose entity holds a field that carries mark — the
product's stores and the other modules', never those of the module the
service belongs to (for a service of the product's, never the product's
own) unless [OwnStores] says so. The notice says which store, which
record and whether it was deleted; the handler reads the record itself
([RecordsOf]). Delivery is at least once and in no set order, retried and
dead-lettered after [MaxDeliveries] attempts: handler must be idempotent,
and it hears the writes it makes itself on another's store — with
OwnStores, never a write its own handler makes. After a stop that was
not clean — the process died with the watch running —, its next start
queues a notice for every record of every store that feeds it, so that
no write a crash took the notice of goes unheard; a deletion whose
notice was lost is not among them. The mark that says a watch runs is
kept in the data directory: an app without one does not catch up (ADR
0178 C6).

	var Content = Service.Watch("content", kit.Moderated, Screen)
	var Posts = Service.Watch("posts", kit.Moderated, Stamp, kit.OwnStores())

symbols.name: Workflow
symbols.spelled: func[E any, S comparable](name string, store *StoreService[E], state func(*E) *S) *WorkflowService[E, S]
symbols.canonical: func[E any, S comparable](name string, store *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.StoreService[E], state func(*E) *S) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.WorkflowService[E, S]
symbols.doc:
Workflow declares a state machine over the entities of store. state returns
a pointer to the entity's state field.

symbols.name: Set
symbols.doc:
Set gives the setting name a value in code, over the environment and the
files: a value of the setting's type, or its text as a variable would
hold it. It is for tests.

symbols.name: SetCookie
symbols.doc:
SetCookie adds a Set-Cookie header to the HTTP response of the endpoint
ctx serves. kit fills what a cookie left zero with safe defaults — Path
"/", HttpOnly, SameSite Lax, and Secure outside dev — so a session cookie
is hardened unless the code says otherwise. In an in-process
[EndpointService.Call] there is no response: the cookie is dropped.

HttpOnly is always set, and Secure always outside dev (and in dev for
SameSite=None, which browsers require): a boolean has no "unset" a default
could fill, and kit chooses the hardened reading. A cookie set more than
once in one response keeps its last value, and cookies set before an error
are sent with the error — clearing a stale session on a 401 works.

symbols.name: SettingConfigurer
symbols.doc: SettingConfigurer configures a setting.

symbols.name: SettingService
symbols.doc:
SettingService is a value the environment gives a service, declared with
[Service.Setting].

symbols.name: Get
symbols.doc:
Get returns the setting's value in the app the service is mounted in —
its default until an app has started with it.

symbols.name: Name
symbols.doc:
Name is the setting's name, its key in a configuration file — in its
module's section, for a module's setting.

symbols.name: SettingValue
symbols.spelled: interface{string | bool | int | int64 | float64 | time.Duration | []string}
symbols.canonical: interface{string | bool | int | int64 | float64 | time.Duration | []string}
symbols.doc: SettingValue is what a setting may hold.

symbols.name: Singleton
symbols.doc:
Singleton keeps one process of the app alive per scope on this machine: the
start takes an exclusive file lock named after scope in the app's runtime
directory (pkg/v1/app/lock: flock, LockFileEx) and holds it until the process
ends. A second process refuses to start with CodeSingletonHeld — for a
daemon's client, the sign to talk to the one that runs. The kernel drops
the lock with a dead process.

symbols.name: SingletonPer
symbols.doc:
SingletonPer keeps one process of the app alive per value of scopes on
this machine — per user, per installed executable, per configuration
directory ([PerUID], [PerExecutable], [PerConfigDir], [PerEnv]) —: the lock
is named after the scopes' key ([ScopeKey]), computed at the start, and
held as Singleton's is. A client that must find the process computes the
same key from the same scopes.

symbols.name: SocketPath
symbols.doc:
SocketPath places the listener's socket at path — absolute, at most 103
bytes — instead of <runtime dir of the app>/<service>-<name>.sock.

IFACE-OPAQUE: ListenerOption is sealed — its one method is unexported —
so only this package makes one, and a caller only passes it to Listen.

symbols.name: SocketPathFor
symbols.spelled: func(product string, service string, name string, scopes ...ScopeValue) (string, error)
symbols.canonical: func(product string, service string, name string, scopes ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.ScopeValue) (string, error)
symbols.doc:
SocketPathFor is the socket of the listener name of service in product —
the binary's name for a role of one, else the app's —, placed by default
and named after scopes (SocketPer): the one rule, for a client of another
process role that does not import the daemon's declarations (D22) — it
names the three words and the scopes its contract states. The service is
its qualified name for a module's.

symbols.name: SocketPer
symbols.doc:
SocketPer names the listener's socket after the value of scopes in this
process — <runtime dir of the app>/<service>-<name>-<key>.sock, the key
being [ScopeKey]'s —: one daemon per user, per executable, per
configuration directory. A client finds it with SocketPathIn or DialIn,
which compute the same key from the same declaration.

IFACE-OPAQUE: ListenerOption is sealed — its one method is unexported —
so only this package makes one, and a caller only passes it to Listen.

symbols.name: Special
symbols.doc: Special marks a field of GDPR art. 9(1) or art. 10.

symbols.name: StaticConfigurer
symbols.doc: StaticConfigurer configures a frontend.

symbols.name: StdioValue
symbols.spelled: struct{In io.Reader; Out io.Writer; Err io.Writer; Interactive bool}
symbols.canonical: struct{In io.Reader; Out io.Writer; Err io.Writer; Interactive bool}

fields.name: In
fields.doc: In is the command's standard input.

fields.name: Out
fields.doc: Out and Err are its standard output and error.

fields.name: Err
fields.doc: Out and Err are its standard output and error.

fields.name: Interactive
fields.doc: Interactive reports whether In is a terminal.

symbols.doc:
StdioValue is where a CLI command reads and writes: the process's own streams
under Main, buffers in a test.

symbols.name: Stop
symbols.doc:
Stop asks the app ctx runs in to end its run: Run returns as it does on a
signal, its stop draining every component — a daemon told "stop" by its
client, on its listener, ends itself so. It returns at once, before the
stop; it reports false when ctx runs in no app — a handler's, a loop's, a
command's context does — or the app does not run.

symbols.name: StoreConfigurer
symbols.doc: StoreConfigurer configures a store.

symbols.name: StoreService
symbols.doc:
StoreService is a typed, keyed collection of entities. Every read returns a copy
and every write stores one: an entity is kept as its JSON encoding, so what
a handler holds can never alias what the store holds, and the memory and
file backends behave identically.

With a data directory (KIT_DATA_DIR; ".kit/data" in dev) the store persists
every write before returning, atomically — a crash never leaves a torn
file — and a write costs one entity, whatever the store holds. Without one,
it lives in memory. A store a database keeps ([Database], [Keeps]) lives
in a table of it, and every call is a round trip. A store is a port (ADR
0004): what it runs on is its engine (store_engine.go) — the SDK's
document store, in memory, in files or over SQL —; kit makes it a node of
the graph, observes every call, and speaks for its refusals. Its writes
join the transaction their context carries ([Transact]).

symbols.name: Count
symbols.doc: Count returns how many entities the store holds.

symbols.name: Delete
symbols.doc:
Delete removes the entity with the given key, or returns a [NotFound] error.
When the store seals at rest and the entity was its person's last record,
their data key goes with it, as with an erasure — at the commit, in a
[Transact] —, once nothing kit keeps still needs it: a held record, or a
former value or version sealed under it, keeps the key.

symbols.name: Diff
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, key string, from uint64, to uint64) ([]Edit, error)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, key string, from uint64, to uint64) ([]github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.Edit, error)
symbols.doc:
Diff returns what changed from the version numbered from to the version
numbered to of the record under key, in RFC 6902's words — add, remove,
replace, each at a JSON pointer — with both values, in the order they
apply: none when the two are the same. A secret member says it changed,
never what. Showing a text's changes line by line is the reader's: the
Studio does it.

symbols.name: Erase
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, key string, reason string) error
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, key string, reason string) error
symbols.doc:
Erase erases one record now, as its retention would: its personal,
special and secret members and its subject cleared — after the store's
Anonymise function has kept what it generalises —, its erased fields
stamped, the rest kept. A held record is refused with a [Conflict] that
names the hold, never a placed hold's reason. reason is journaled, for
whoever runs the product.

symbols.name: Filter
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, keep func(T) bool) ([]T, error)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, keep func(T) bool) ([]T, error)
symbols.doc:
Filter returns the entities keep accepts, ordered by key. It reads every
entity: an index is the way to avoid it.

symbols.name: Find
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, index string, key string) ([]T, error)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, index string, key string) ([]T, error)
symbols.doc:
Find returns the entities indexed under key, ordered by their store key. It
reads any index, unique or not; no entity is an empty slice, not an error.

symbols.name: Former
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, key string, pointer string) ([]Former, error)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, key string, pointer string) ([]github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.Former, error)
symbols.doc:
Former returns the former values of the field at pointer — its JSON
pointer (RFC 6901), "/email" — in the record under key, newest first:
each with when it was replaced and by whom. A secret field's former values
say when they changed, never what they were: their Value is empty. A field
that keeps no former values is an [Invalid] error, a missing record a
[NotFound].

symbols.name: Get
symbols.doc: Get returns the entity with the given key, or a [NotFound] error.

symbols.name: Hold
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, key string, reason string) error
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, key string, reason string) error
symbols.doc:
Hold places a legal hold on the record under key: neither the retention,
nor a person's erasure, nor Delete touches it until [StoreService.Release] lifts
it. reason says why — an authority's request, a case under litigation —
and is kept for whoever runs the product, never shown in the Studio.
Holding a held record again replaces its reason.

symbols.name: Insert
symbols.doc: Insert stores a new entity; it is a [Conflict] error when the key exists.

symbols.name: List
symbols.doc: List returns every entity, ordered by key.

symbols.name: Lookup
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, index string, key string) (T, error)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, index string, key string) (T, error)
symbols.doc:
Lookup returns the entity whose key in the unique index is key, or a
[NotFound] error. Asking a non-unique index is an [Invalid] error: use
[StoreService.Find].

symbols.name: Passwords
symbols.doc:
Passwords declares the password policy of one secret field of the store's
entity; field names it — kit calls it on a zero entity to find which. The
field then only ever holds the password's hash, a PHC string, or nothing
before a first password; a write that puts anything else in it is
refused. A field that is not secret refuses the start, as does a second
policy on the same field.

symbols.name: Put
symbols.doc: Put stores the entity, replacing any entity with the same key.

symbols.name: Release
symbols.doc:
Release lifts the hold on the record under key: the retention takes it up
again, from where its instants say. A record no hold keeps is a
[NotFound] error.

symbols.name: Restore
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, key string, number uint64, fields ...string) (T, error)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, key string, number uint64, fields ...string) (T, error)
symbols.doc:
Restore writes the version numbered number of the record under key back,
as a new version: history is never rewritten. It restores the whole
version, or only the fields named by JSON pointer (RFC 6901) — "/title" —,
as WordPress restores some fields of a revision. It keeps the record's
workflow state, which its workflow owns, and every secret member:
restoring an account never brings back an old password past its policy,
and naming one of them is an [Invalid] error. A unique index the restored
record breaks refuses it with a [Conflict], and nothing changes. It
returns the record as restored.

symbols.name: Revision

symbols.doc:

symbols.name: Publish
symbols.doc:
Publish sends msg to every subscription. It returns once every
subscription's queue has accepted the message; delivery happens later.
Inside a transaction ([Transact], a command's) the message is encoded now
and queued at the commit: in the transaction, just before it commits, for
a subscription whose queue lives on the transaction's database — a queue
that refuses it then fails the transaction —, once it committed for the
others. A rollback drops it.

symbols.name: Transact
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, fn func(context.Context) error) error
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, fn func(context.Context) error) error
symbols.doc:
Transact runs fn in one transaction and returns fn's error: nil commits
what fn wrote, an error undoes it — a panic too, which then continues.

	err := kit.Transact(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error {
		if _, err := Cases.Update(ctx, id, closeCase); err != nil {
			return err // what this function wrote is undone
		}
		if err := Decisions.Insert(ctx, d); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return Changes.Publish(ctx, Closed{ID: id}) // held: queued at the commit
	})

A transaction belongs to one database: the one its first store call
reaches — at its first call on a database, at its first write on the data
directory, which counts as one, memory with it. Inside it, a store of
another database is read as usual; writing one is refused ([Invalid],
[CodeTransactionSpan]). A Transact inside another is a savepoint: its
failure undoes its own writes, and the outer transaction goes on if its
caller handles the error.

What leaves the process waits for the outermost commit: a topic's
publish, a queued command's dispatch, a mail — whose outbox ID [Mailer.Send]
returns at once —, a watch's notice, the store's write hooks that wake
workflows and loops, a workflow's OnTransition hooks. Each is checked when
it is made, so a caller's mistake returns to the caller; a rollback drops
them, and a savepoint's rollback its own. A publish, a dispatch, a mail or a
notice whose queue lives on the transaction's database — the one that
keeps the service of its subscription, command, mailer or watch, by a
store's rules — is written in the transaction, just before it commits, a
mail sealed under kit's data-key: a queue that refuses
it fails the transaction, every write undone, and Transact returns the
refusal. Every other one leaves after the commit: one a queue refuses then
is logged and reported, and the commit stands; a process that dies
between the commit and the release loses what was held.

On a database the transaction is the database's own, at its default
isolation. On the data directory and in memory kit keeps its own: it takes
the data's writer turn — one transaction at a time; a write outside any
waits for it, and such writes share the turn among themselves —, its
writes land at once, and an error writes each entity's previous value
back, newest first. It is atomic against an error, not against a crash,
and a reader may see a write before its commit. A store kept in memory by
[InMemory] — a cache — is in no transaction: its writes land and stay.

A command's handler runs in one already ([NoTransaction] opts out), and
so does a workflow's transition.

symbols.name: WorkflowService
symbols.doc:
WorkflowService is a state machine over the entities of one store: the states an
entity goes through, and the arrows between them. It is declared as data —
which is why the diagram can draw it exactly — and it runs four kinds of
transitions:

  - event transitions ([WorkflowService.On]), fired by code with [WorkflowService.Fire];
  - timer transitions ([WorkflowService.After]), fired by the workflow's own loop
    once an entity has spent a duration in a state;
  - timer transitions at an instant the entity carries ([WorkflowService.At]) — a
    due date, a deadline — fired by the same loop when it comes;
  - guard transitions ([WorkflowService.When]), fired by the same loop as soon as
    a condition on the entity holds.

The SDK's state-machine engine runs it (statemachine). Its loop never
polls: it keeps an agenda of the transitions due, sleeps until the
earliest, and a write of the store — which may bring one forward — wakes
it. A workflow with nothing due does not run at all. Transitions of one
entity run one at a time, of different entities at once.

The entity's state lives in the entity itself (the state function returns
a pointer to it), so the store stays the single source of truth; the
engine keeps, beside it, when each entity entered its state and the
history of its transitions — in the workflow's file under the data
directory, so a timer keeps counting across a restart.

symbols.spelled: func[D Delay](event string, d D, from S, to S) *WorkflowService[E, S]
symbols.canonical: func[D github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.Delay](event string, d D, from S, to S) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.WorkflowService[E, S]
symbols.doc:
After declares a timer transition: an entity that has spent d in state from
moves to state to, fired by the workflow's own loop. d is a duration, or a

symbols.doc:
At declares a timer transition at an instant the entity carries — a due
date, a deadline: an entity in state from moves to state to once the time
instant returns has come; false means no instant for now. kit asks again
each time the entity is written, and the workflow's own loop sleeps until
the earliest instant.

cancels the transition, and so does a panic — reported as
[CodeWorkflowHookPanic], the entity free for the next transition. fn may

and must not fire this workflow, which is refused
