symbols.doc:
HoldSubject places a legal hold on every record whose subject is one of
ids, in every store of the app: an authority's request about a person.
It holds the records they have now; a record written later is not held.
reason is kept as Store.Hold keeps it.

symbols.name: IdleStop
symbols.doc:
IdleStop makes a daemon stop itself once, for d, no connection was open on
any of its listeners and no activity of its services (Service.Activity)
said it was busy: a daemon launched on demand by its clients ends when
they stop coming. It is refused outside the daemon profile.

symbols.name: InMemory
symbols.doc:
InMemory keeps data in memory. On an app, it overrides the data directory
for every store and queue — KIT_DATA_DIR, and a [DataDir] given before it:
what a test wants. On a store, it keeps that store in memory even when the
app has a data directory.

symbols.name: Index
symbols.spelled: func[T any](name string, keys func(T) []string) StoreOption
symbols.doc:
Index declares an index where an entity may have several keys and a key
several entities — the users a task is shared with. [Store].Find reads it.
Empty keys are not indexed.

symbols.name: Invalid
symbols.doc: Invalid reports a request the caller must change before retrying (400).

symbols.name: Job
symbols.doc:
Job is scheduled work: a piece of the daemon's internal loop. It runs on
the SDK scheduler, whose decisions about time are documented rather than
emergent: a fire that is due while the previous run of the same job is
still going is skipped and counted, and a missed deadline is skipped and
counted, never caught up.

symbols.name: KeepVersions
symbols.doc:
KeepVersions is how many versions of a generated secret a rotation leaves,
the new one included: at least 2, so that what the version it replaces
sealed or signed still opens and verifies. Cover the longest-lived box or
signature in flight: its lifetime divided by the interval, plus one.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: Keepable
symbols.doc:
Keepable is what a database keeps: a service — every store it declares —,
a store, or a module (ADR 0008) — every store of its services.

symbols.name: Keeps
symbols.doc:
Keeps says what the database keeps: a service's stores, a store, a
module's stores. The most precise wins: a store kept by name, then its
service, then its module, then the default database — the one declared
without Keeps —, then the data directory, then memory. [InMemory] wins
over all of them, on the app as on a store.

symbols.name: Listen
symbols.doc:
Listen sets the listening address, instead of KIT_ADDR or PORT. ":0" picks
a free port; App.URL tells which.

symbols.name: ListenHandler
symbols.doc:
ListenHandler serves one connection of a [Listener] until it returns; the
connection is closed after it. conn.Peer says who connected, as the kernel
says where it can (pkg/v1/proc/ipc).

symbols.name: Listener
symbols.doc:
Listener is an inbound port that is not HTTP: a private socket on this
machine — a Unix socket in a directory only the product's account can
reach, the kernel naming the peer on Linux (ADR 0148) — speaking a
versioned contract. It is how a daemon profile serves its clients, and how
two process roles of one binary talk (D22): through the contract, never
through each other's code.

symbols.name: ListenerOption
symbols.doc: ListenerOption tunes a listener.

symbols.name: LockWaiter
symbols.doc:
LockWaiter is an [Engine] whose connections wait a bounded time for a lock
another connection holds — SQLite's busy timeout —, a sibling of Engine
(ADR 0178 C2). kit opens such an engine's pool with OpenWaiting instead
of Open, and gives it a wait under <name>-timeout, so that a lost race on
the lock comes back as the engine's refusal before the call's own
deadline. An engine that does not implement it keeps its own wait.

symbols.name: Log
symbols.doc:
Log returns the app's logger, for the node ctx runs inside. In dev, every
record it writes inside a span is also kept beside that span, so the
Studio shows a request's logs with its trace.

symbols.name: Logs
symbols.doc: Logs sends the app's logs to w instead of standard error.

symbols.name: Loop
symbols.doc:
Loop is a declared loop of the daemon: kit owns the wait, the product owns
the work. Its wake sources — a period, a deadline the product computes, a
topic — are data, so the diagram draws exactly what wakes it; kit runs it on
its own goroutine, one run at a time, observes every run, and restarts it
after a panic.

symbols.name: LoopOption
symbols.doc: LoopOption configures a declared loop.

symbols.name: MailAttempts
symbols.doc:
MailAttempts is how many deliveries a message gets before it is
dead-lettered. The default is 6, backing off from one second.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: Mailer
symbols.doc:
Mailer is outbound mail: a durable outbox and the transport that empties
it. [Mailer].Send only queues — it returns once the message is safely in
the outbox — and the mailer's own loop hands each message to the transport,
retrying a failure and dead-lettering a message after its last attempt.

The transport is the SDK's mail package: SMTP when the mail connector's
secret smtp-url is set — KIT_SMTP_URL, smtp://user:password@host:587?tls=
starttls|implicit|none — and otherwise the capture transport, which keeps
every message for the Studio's mailbox and for tests ([Mailer].Captured)
and delivers nothing. Outside dev, the capture transport is reported as a
warning. The URL is read again before every delivery: replacing it where
it lives — a new version in the store, a new file behind
KIT_SMTP_URL_FILE — takes effect at the next mail.

symbols.name: MailerOption
symbols.doc: MailerOption configures a mailer.

symbols.name: Mark
symbols.doc:
Mark is what a module looks for in the product's fields: kit.Personal,
kit.Special or kit.Moderated. There is no mark for public or secret:
there is nothing to find in the first, and nothing may watch the second.

symbols.name: MaxBody
symbols.doc:
MaxBody bounds the request body the endpoint reads. The default is
[DefaultMaxBody].

symbols.name: MaxDeliveries
symbols.doc:
MaxDeliveries is how many attempts a message gets before it is
dead-lettered — a subscription's, or a queued command's. The default is
5.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: Migrations
symbols.doc:
Migrations are migrations, values of the SDK's sql.Migration, run when
the database starts (<name>-migrate: start) or by `<product> migrate up`,
kit's own first, each set under its own version table — and so its own
lock. On MySQL a DDL statement commits by itself: write one per migration.

Given to [Database], they are the product's, under schema_migrations.
Given to [NewModule], they are the module's (ADR 0008), for the data it
keeps outside kit's stores: run on the database that keeps the module,
under <module>_migrations.

symbols.name: MinLength
symbols.doc:
MinLength refuses a password shorter than n characters, counted as NIST
counts them: one per Unicode code point. The default is 15, NIST's figure
for a password used alone; 8 is the floor NIST allows with a second
factor, and a smaller n is refused. There is no composition rule, ever:
NIST says SHALL NOT.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: Moderated
symbols.doc: Moderated marks content others see and a moderator may act on.

symbols.name: Module
symbols.doc:
Module is a set of services a product mounts as one: [NewModule] declares
it, [App].With or [Mount] mounts it.

symbols.name: ModulePart
symbols.doc:
ModulePart is what a module is made of: its services, the modules it
requires ([Requires]), and the migrations of the data it keeps outside
kit's stores ([Migrations]).

symbols.name: Mount
symbols.doc:
Mount mounts module m with options: [Prefix] serves its routes elsewhere
than "/<module>/", [Bind] chooses what one of its ports calls.

	app := kit.NewApp("vigie", identity.Service).
		With(kit.Mount(moderation.Module, kit.Prefix("/"), kit.Bind(moderation.Enforcer, posts.EnforceAPI)))

A module is mounted once per app: mounted again, its prefix is the last
one given, and its bindings join the others, the last of a port winning.

symbols.name: MountOption
symbols.doc: MountOption configures the mount of a module: [Prefix], [Bind].

symbols.name: Name
symbols.doc:
Name overrides the endpoint's name, which otherwise is its handler's
function name, or its route when the handler is a function literal.

symbols.name: NewApp
symbols.doc:
NewApp declares the product named name, made of services. A module's
services come with the module: [App].With mounts it.

symbols.name: NewBinary
symbols.doc: NewBinary declares the binary named name.

symbols.name: NewID
symbols.doc:
NewID returns a new identifier with the given prefix: a TypeID, time
ordered, like "todo_01k5zq7m3xe8tvbfg0s7zr4w6c". The prefix must be one to
sixty-three lower-case letters, with '_' only between two letters; any
other prefix is a programming error and panics.

symbols.name: NewModule
symbols.doc:
NewModule declares a module named name — lower-case letters, digits and
dashes, starting with a letter; "kit", "external" and "schema" are kit's — that doc
describes, made of parts: its services, which it adopts, the modules it
requires ([Requires]), and the migrations of the data it keeps outside
kit's stores ([Migrations]), run on the database that keeps it. Declare it
as a package-level variable of the one package a product imports:

	var Module = kit.NewModule("moderation",
		"Reports and moderation under the DSA.\n\nfr: Signalements et modération selon le DSA.",
		intake.Service, desk.Service, kit.Requires(identity.Module))

A service a module lists is its own: what it declared so far is renamed,
and what it declares later is born qualified. Listing a service links its
package; a service is a module's only, and a module's services take
declarations from the module's own Go module only.

symbols.name: NewService
symbols.doc:
NewService declares a service. name must be lower-case letters, digits and
dashes, starting with a letter; doc is one sentence saying what it owns.

symbols.name: NewTicker
symbols.doc:
NewTicker is a ticker of period d on the app's clock, for a loop written by
hand ([Service].Go): a test's manual clock drives it like every timer kit
runs itself, where a time.Ticker would tick on the wall clock whatever the
test does. It panics on a non-positive d, as time.NewTicker does.

symbols.name: NoTransaction
symbols.doc:
NoTransaction runs a command outside a transaction of its own: its
writes land as its handler makes them, and its effects leave when made —
a failed command may have written or announced something. On the data
directory and in memory, where a writing command's transaction takes the
writer turn, it lets such commands run side by side. Dispatched inside
another command, it still runs in that one's transaction.

symbols.name: NotCommon
symbols.doc:
NotCommon refuses a password among the ten thousand most common ones —
the SDK's password.IsCommon, which compares them without regard to case —:
the blocklist NIST SP 800-63B-4 requires a verifier to check, beyond the
three thousand OWASP ASVS 5.0 (6.2.4) asks for. Every policy checks it (ADR
0007 §2: on by default once the SDK has the list); the option says so
where a policy is declared. Beside NIST's fifteen characters the list has
little left to refuse; beside a shorter MinLength, it matters.

symbols.name: NotFound
symbols.doc: NotFound reports that the addressed resource does not exist (404).

symbols.name: NotReused
symbols.doc:
NotReused refuses a password that the current hash, or any of the n
former ones, verifies — n from 1 to 100. It is a compliance policy, off by
default: PCI DSS asks for it, OWASP ASVS 4.0.3 asks most products not to
impose it. kit keeps the field's last n hashes, so it implies history=n,
and a tag whose history is smaller than n is refused.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: Now
symbols.doc:
Now returns the app's time: the system clock, or the clock a test gave
with [Clock]. Product code that compares with a deadline reads it rather
than time.Now, so that a test's manual clock reaches it.

symbols.name: Operation
symbols.doc:
Operation takes a typed request and answers a typed response: an
endpoint, a port — and, with ADR 0005, a command or a query. It is what
[Fallback] and [Bind] give a port, and what [Replace] replaces in a test;
a request or a response of other types does not compile. Its methods are
unexported: only kit implements it.

Every operation is a node of the graph, and runs in a span of its own
through its whole pipeline — authentication, validation, policies, the
Studio's mocks — whoever calls it.

symbols.name: OperationOption
symbols.doc:
OperationOption configures an endpoint, a command or a query alike: the
authentication it asks for ([Auth], [AuthOptional]) and the policies in
front of its handler ([RateLimit], [RateLimitPerClient], [Timeout],
[Bulkhead]).

symbols.name: Optional
symbols.doc:
Optional makes a provided secret one the product can do without — the key
of a feature that stays off while nobody gives it. A start where it is set
nowhere goes on; [Secret].Present says whether it is set now, and a use of
it while it is absent — [Secret].Value, Seal, Open, Sign or Verify —
answers an error errs.HasCode matches with [CodeSecretMissing]. It is read
where it lives at every use, as every provided secret is: given later —
`secrets set` in the environment's store, a new content in the file its
_FILE variable names —, it is found at its next use. A generated secret
is kit's to make and never absent: Optional with [Generated] is refused.

symbols.name: OwnStores
symbols.doc:
OwnStores lets a watch ([Service].Watch) hear the stores of its own
module too — the product's own, for a watch of the product's —, which a
watch never hears by default. Such a watch never hears the writes its own
handler makes, in its handler's context — a handler that writes what it
watches, a screening that stamps the record it screened, would otherwise
hear itself forever —; a write the handler only causes, later and
elsewhere — a queued command's handling, a topic's delivery — is heard.
A subscription to a topic refuses it: a topic has no stores.

symbols.name: Parallelism
symbols.doc:
Parallelism is how many messages are handled at once — a subscription's,
or a queued command's. The default is 1.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: PasswordOption
symbols.doc: PasswordOption configures a password policy: [MinLength], [NotReused].

symbols.name: PasswordPolicy
symbols.doc:
PasswordPolicy is the policy of one secret field that holds a password's
hash: how long a password is at least, and how many former passwords it
refuses. [Store].Passwords declares it; Set, Change and Verify apply it.

symbols.name: PerConfigDir
symbols.doc:
PerConfigDir is the user's configuration directory (os.UserConfigDir):
one process per configuration home.

symbols.name: PerEnv
symbols.doc:
PerEnv is the environment variable name, else fallback when it is unset
or empty; a leading "~/" in either is the user's home directory. The
status line's is PerEnv("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", "~/.claude"): one daemon per
Claude configuration.

symbols.name: PerExecutable
symbols.doc:
PerExecutable is the running executable's path, links resolved: one
process per installed copy of the binary.

symbols.name: PerUID
symbols.doc:
PerUID is the current user: one process per user of the machine (its
UID on Unix, its SID on Windows).

symbols.name: Personal
symbols.doc:
Personal marks a field that holds data about a person: personal,
special, or a record's subject.

symbols.name: PersonalData
symbols.doc: PersonalData is a person's data as kit.Export gives it.

symbols.name: Port
symbols.doc:
Port is an operation a service needs and does not implement: a typed
request, a typed response, a name. Declare it with [Service].Port, and
call it with [Port].Call as an endpoint is called: validated, observed,
drawn.

What a port calls is decided when the app starts, by one rule the static
analysis shares: the app's [Bind], else the one [Service].Implement among
the services the app mounts, else the port's own [Fallback]. The start
refuses a port it cannot bind, with every other problem at once.

A port is how a service reaches what it cannot import — a module its
host's content, a service another that imports it — the consumer owning
the contract.

symbols.name: PortOption
symbols.doc: PortOption configures a port: [Fallback].

symbols.name: Prefix
symbols.doc:
Prefix serves a module's routes under prefix — "/trust/" — instead of
"/<module>/"; "/" shares the product's route space, where a route both
declare is refused as any two are. A prefix starts and ends with '/', and
never lies under /_kit/.

symbols.name: Principal
symbols.doc:
Principal is what the app's auth data says about the caller to the
SDK's authz: the attributes [Command].Allow and [Query].Allow hand a
policy — the caller's roles, its groups. Auth data that does not
implement it gives none, and every Allow refuses: the start warns of it.

	type Me struct{ Roles []string }

	func (m Me) Attrs() []authz.Attr { return []authz.Attr{authz.AttrStrings("roles", m.Roles...)} }

kit calls the caller a principal: in kit, a subject is the person
personal data is about (ADR 0006).

symbols.name: Privacy
symbols.doc:
Privacy is kit's own service: the legal holds and the privacy journal of
an app that keeps personal data. kit mounts a copy of it — named
kit.privacy, a name no service of a product can take — in every app whose
stores keep personal data or declare a retention, before the product's
services. Its stores stay in the data directory unless the product places
them (ADR 0004). A product never mounts it itself.

symbols.name: Profile
symbols.doc:
Profile selects the app's process profile: model.ProfileServer (the
default), model.ProfileDaemon or model.ProfileCLI.

symbols.name: Purpose
symbols.doc:
Purpose says why the store keeps its records (GDPR art. 30(1)(b)): the
register lists it, and a person's export carries it.

symbols.name: Query
symbols.doc:
Query reads and changes nothing: a typed input, a typed result, and one
handler — the one declared with it. Declare it with [Service].Query; ask it
with [Query].Ask from any building block, which draws an asks edge from
the caller; give it a route with [Query].Expose. The static analysis warns
of a query whose code writes a store, fires a workflow, publishes, sends a
mail or dispatches a command.

A question runs, in this order: the caller's user when the query asks for
one ([Auth], implied by [Query].Allow), the input's validate tags, the
policies, the authorization ([Query].Allow, then [Query].Authorize), then
the handler, on the caller's goroutine.

symbols.name: QueryOption
symbols.doc:
QueryOption configures a query: the options every operation takes —
[Auth], [AuthOptional], [RateLimit], [RateLimitPerClient], [Timeout],
[Bulkhead].

symbols.name: Queued
symbols.doc:
Queued sends a command to the background. Dispatch returns once the
command's own queue accepted it — a file queue under the data directory,
memory without one —, and a consumer handles it, [Parallelism] at a time,
retried up to [MaxDeliveries] attempts (5) — half a second after the first
failure, the wait doubling after each, never more than a minute —, then
dead-lettered; a dispatch that does not decode is dead-lettered at its
first failure, since no retry makes it decode. It answers nothing: its
result is [Empty], and exposed, it answers 202 Accepted.

Delivery is at least once: Queued is the product's promise that the
handler tolerates a redelivery, and a [Command].Key narrows the duplicates
without removing them. The handler runs in the dispatcher's trace, as the
user who dispatched it ([UserID]); what the auth handler said about that
user is not queued. A queued command's input is a contract with the
messages already queued: add a field, never rename one.

symbols.name: RateLimit
symbols.doc:
RateLimit puts a token bucket in front of the handler: perSecond tokens a
second, up to burst at once. An empty bucket answers 429 at once. It is the
SDK's resilience rate limiter.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: RateLimitPerClient
symbols.doc:
RateLimitPerClient gives every client of an endpoint a token bucket of its
own: perSecond tokens a second, up to burst at once. A client is the
authenticated user when there is one, and the client's address otherwise
([ClientIP]); in-process calls through [Endpoint].Call share one bucket. One
client emptying its bucket is answered 429; the others are not — which is
what a sign-in endpoint needs, where one shared bucket would let a single
client lock everybody out.

Buckets unused for ten minutes are forgotten, and at most 10 000 are kept:
the least recently used goes first. It is the SDK's keyed rate limiter.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: ReadModel
symbols.doc:
ReadModel marks a store as derived from others (ADR 0005): written by
projections — the subscriptions that keep it from the write side's
events —, read by queries. It changes nothing of how the store runs; the
diagram draws it on its domain's read side, and the static analysis warns
of a read model written by anything but a subscription. kit's topics are
queues, not logs: a read model cannot be replayed from its events, and one
fed by a topic lags the commands that feed it — a query that must read its
own writes reads the write side.

	var Summaries = Service.Store("summaries", Summary.Key, kit.ReadModel())

symbols.name: Records
symbols.doc:
Records is one store's records without their type. Get returns a record
without its secret members; Keys lists the records' keys, to a module that
watches the store; EraseFields and Delete take a reason and are refused on a
held record. Each call is a span on the store's node and an entry in the
privacy journal.

symbols.name: RecordsOf
symbols.doc:
RecordsOf is [App].Records for code the app runs and that does not hold
it — a module's watch, its endpoints: the records port of the store whose
node ID is store, in the app ctx runs in. Outside a running app it is an
[Unavailable] error.

	func Screen(ctx context.Context, w kit.Written) error {
		recs, err := kit.RecordsOf(ctx, w.Store)
		…
		record, err := recs.Get(ctx, w.Key)

symbols.name: Replace
symbols.spelled: func[Req, Resp any](op ikit.Operation[Req, Resp], fn func(context.Context, Req) (Resp, error)) AppOption
symbols.canonical: func[Req, Resp any](op github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit.Operation[Req, Resp], fn func(context.Context, Req) (Resp, error)) github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/kit.AppOption
symbols.doc:
Replace runs fn in place of op's code, in the app it is given to: an
endpoint's handler — or, with ADR 0005, a command's or a query's — or what
a port calls. It replaces the code, not the mechanics: authentication,
decoding, validation and the policies still run, and a replaced port needs
no binding, so a module's tests run without a host. fn takes op's request
and returns its response, or it does not compile.

A replaced run's span carries mock: replace, and runtime.mocks lists the
replacement. It is for tests: the start refuses it in a program go test
did not build — neither a production binary nor kit dev can carry one.
Given twice for one operation, the last wins.

	app := App.With(kit.Replace(apps.AppAPI, func(ctx context.Context, in apps.IDInput) (apps.Profile, error) {
		return apps.Profile{ID: in.AppID}, nil
	}))

symbols.name: Required
symbols.doc:
Required drops a setting's default: a start without a value for it fails,
saying where to give one.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: Requires
symbols.doc:
Requires says the module needs other: an app that mounts the module and
not other mounts other at its defaults, and starts it first. The Go import
this takes makes a cycle impossible. A collaboration a module can do
without is a port with a fallback instead ([Fallback]).

symbols.name: RetentionByProduct
symbols.doc:
RetentionByProduct says the product keeps the store's retention itself:
its own code erases and deletes what it no longer needs — a record whose
life the product's own rules end, a lifecycle kit cannot read from the
entity. limits says, in the product's words, for how long and how, which
the register publishes as the store's time limits (GDPR art. 30(1)(f));
"" says only that the product keeps them.

kit then runs no retention for the store, and warns of neither a missing
retention nor a missing subject. Its classified fields keep every other
promise: sealed at rest, never shown, exported with their person — when
the store names one — and erased by kit.Erase and Store.Erase. It goes
with kit.Purpose, kit.HeldUntil, kit.Anonymise and kit.DeleteOnErasure;
with kit.EraseAfter, kit.EraseAt, kit.DeleteAfter or kit.DeleteAt it is
refused: a store's retention is kit's or the product's, never both.

symbols.name: Revision
symbols.doc:
Revision is one version of a record a store with [Revisions] keeps: its
number — from 1, never given twice while the record exists —, when the
write that made it ran, on the app's clock, zero for a record stored before
its store kept revisions; who made it — the caller's [UserID], empty for a
write with no user —; which command made it — its node ID, empty outside a
command —; and the record as it was, its secret members zeroed.

symbols.name: Revisions
symbols.doc:
Revisions keeps the n previous versions of each record of the store, n
from 1 to 100, as WordPress keeps a post's revisions: every write that
changes a record makes a version, numbered from 1 and never renumbered,
stamped with when it was made, the caller's user and the command that
made it; the oldest beyond n are pruned by the write that makes a newer
one, unless a legal hold keeps the record.

	var Pages = Service.Store("pages", Page.Key, kit.Revisions(20))

	revs, err := Pages.Revisions(ctx, id)                            // newest first
	edits, err := Pages.Diff(ctx, id, revs[3].Number, revs[0].Number)
	page, err := Pages.Restore(ctx, id, revs[3].Number)              // a new version
	page, err = Pages.Restore(ctx, id, revs[3].Number, "/title")     // the title only

A store with Revisions(n) holds up to n+1 times its records: in memory
with the store in the data directory, in the table <table>___vs on a
database, which kit's migrations create.

symbols.name: Root
symbols.doc:
Root serves the sub-directory dir of the file system rather than its root —
"assets" for a //go:embed assets directive.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: RotateEvery
symbols.doc:
RotateEvery is how often kit makes a new version of a generated secret.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: Routine
symbols.doc:
Routine is a loop written by hand: a function that runs until its context
ends. kit starts it with the app, cancels its context on shutdown and waits
for it, restarts it after an error or a panic — backing off from one second
to one minute — and reads its select statements to draw what it waits on.

symbols.name: Scope
symbols.doc:
Scope is one part of a path computed at the start: the user, the
executable, a configuration directory. Two processes share a singleton or
a socket when every scope gives them the same value.

symbols.name: ScopeKey
symbols.doc:
ScopeKey is the name the scopes give in this process: 16 hex digits of the
SHA-256 of their values. A client computes the key the daemon computed
from the same declaration, and so finds its lock or its socket.

symbols.name: Secret
symbols.doc:
Secret is a secret the product declares: provided by the operator — an SMTP
URL, an API token — or generated by kit — a signing or sealing key — and
rotated on its schedule.

symbols.name: SecretOption
symbols.doc: SecretOption configures a secret.

symbols.name: SecretStore
symbols.doc:
SecretStore keeps the secrets in store instead of the environment's: a
test gives a store holding what its provided secrets hold. The
environment's variables are still read first.

symbols.name: Service
Set
symbols.spelled: func[V any](name string, value V) AppOption
symbols.doc:
Set gives the setting name a value in code, over the environment and the
files: a value of the setting's type, or its text as a variable would
hold it. It is for tests.

symbols.name: SetCookie
symbols.doc:
SetCookie adds a Set-Cookie header to the HTTP response of the endpoint
ctx serves. kit fills what a cookie left zero with safe defaults — Path
"/", HttpOnly, SameSite Lax, and Secure outside dev — so a session cookie
is hardened unless the code says otherwise. In an in-process
[Endpoint].Call there is no response: the cookie is dropped.

HttpOnly is always set, and Secure always outside dev (and in dev for
SameSite=None, which browsers require): a boolean has no "unset" a default
could fill, and kit chooses the hardened reading. A cookie set more than
once in one response keeps its last value, and cookies set before an error
are sent with the error — clearing a stale session on a 401 works.

symbols.name: Setting
symbols.doc:
Setting is a value the environment gives a service, declared with
[Service].Setting.

symbols.name: SettingOption
symbols.doc: SettingOption configures a setting.

symbols.name: SettingValue
symbols.doc: SettingValue is what a setting may hold.

symbols.name: Singleton
symbols.doc:
Singleton keeps one process of the app alive per scope on this machine: the
start takes an exclusive file lock named after scope in the app's runtime
directory (pkg/v1/app/lock: flock, LockFileEx) and holds it until the process
ends. A second process refuses to start with CodeSingletonHeld — for a
daemon's client, the sign to talk to the one that runs. The kernel drops
the lock with a dead process.

symbols.name: SingletonPer
symbols.doc:
SingletonPer keeps one process of the app alive per value of scopes on
this machine — per user, per installed executable, per configuration
directory ([PerUID], [PerExecutable], [PerConfigDir], [PerEnv]) —: the lock
is named after the scopes' key ([ScopeKey]), computed at the start, and
held as Singleton's is. A client that must find the process computes the
same key from the same scopes.

symbols.name: SocketPath
symbols.doc:
SocketPath places the listener's socket at path — absolute, at most 103
bytes — instead of <runtime dir of the app>/<service>-<name>.sock.

IFACE-OPAQUE: ListenerOption is sealed — its one method is unexported —
so only this package makes one, and a caller only passes it to Listen.

symbols.name: SocketPathFor
symbols.spelled: func(product string, service string, name string, scopes ...Scope) (string, error)
symbols.canonical: func(product string, service string, name string, scopes ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/kit.Scope) (string, error)
symbols.doc:
SocketPathFor is the socket of the listener name of service in product —
the binary's name for a role of one, else the app's —, placed by default
and named after scopes (SocketPer): the one rule, for a client of another
process role that does not import the daemon's declarations (D22) — it
names the three words and the scopes its contract states. The service is
its qualified name for a module's.

symbols.name: SocketPer
symbols.doc:
SocketPer names the listener's socket after the value of scopes in this
process — <runtime dir of the app>/<service>-<name>-<key>.sock, the key
being [ScopeKey]'s —: one daemon per user, per executable, per
configuration directory. A client finds it with SocketPathIn or DialIn,
which compute the same key from the same declaration.

IFACE-OPAQUE: ListenerOption is sealed — its one method is unexported —
so only this package makes one, and a caller only passes it to Listen.

symbols.name: Special
symbols.doc: Special marks a field of GDPR art. 9(1) or art. 10.

symbols.name: StaticOption
symbols.doc: StaticOption configures a frontend.

symbols.name: Stdio
symbols.doc:
Stdio is where a CLI command reads and writes: the process's own streams
under Main, buffers in a test.

symbols.name: Stop
symbols.doc:
Stop asks the app ctx runs in to end its run: Run returns as it does on a
signal, its stop draining every component — a daemon told "stop" by its
client, on its listener, ends itself so. It returns at once, before the
stop; it reports false when ctx runs in no app — a handler's, a loop's, a
command's context does — or the app does not run.

symbols.name: Store
symbols.doc:
Store is a typed, keyed collection of entities. Every read returns a copy
and every write stores one: an entity is kept as its JSON encoding, so what
a handler holds can never alias what the store holds, and the memory and
file backends behave identically.

With a data directory (KIT_DATA_DIR; ".kit/data" in dev) the store persists
every write before returning, atomically — a crash never leaves a torn
file — and a write costs one entity, whatever the store holds. Without one,
it lives in memory. A store is a port (ADR 0004): what it runs on is its
engine (store_engine.go), today the SDK's document store (docstore); kit
makes it a node of the graph, observes every call, and speaks for its
refusals.

symbols.name: StoreOption
symbols.doc: StoreOption configures a store.

symbols.name: Studio
symbols.doc:
Studio switches the Studio on or off in dev. It is always off in
production.

symbols.name: Subscription
symbols.doc:
Subscription consumes a topic: its handler runs once per message, at least
once, retried on error, and dead-lettered after MaxDeliveries attempts.

symbols.name: SubscriptionOption
symbols.doc: SubscriptionOption configures a subscription.

symbols.name: Telemetry
symbols.doc:
Telemetry exports the app's telemetry on the private socket at path —
absolute, and short enough for a Unix socket (pkg/v1/proc/ipc) — admitting the groups gids besides the
product's own account. It wins over KIT_TELEMETRY.

symbols.name: Timeout
symbols.doc:
Timeout cancels the handler's context after d and answers 504. It is the
SDK's resilience timeout.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: Topic
symbols.doc:
Topic is an asynchronous channel of messages of type T. Every subscription
receives every message, at least once: a subscription's handler must
tolerate a redelivery.

symbols.name: Transact
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, fn func(context.Context) error) error
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, fn func(context.Context) error) error
symbols.doc:
Transact runs fn in one transaction and returns fn's error: nil commits
what fn wrote, an error undoes it — a panic too, which then continues.

	err := kit.Transact(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error {
		if _, err := Cases.Update(ctx, id, closeCase); err != nil {
			return err // what this function wrote is undone
		}
		if err := Decisions.Insert(ctx, d); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return Changes.Publish(ctx, Closed{ID: id}) // held: queued at the commit
	})

A transaction belongs to one database: the one its first store call
reaches — at its first call on a database, at its first write on the data
directory, which counts as one, memory with it. Inside it, a store of
another database is read as usual; writing one is refused ([Invalid],
[CodeTransactionSpan]). A Transact inside another is a savepoint: its
failure undoes its own writes, and the outer transaction goes on if its
caller handles the error.

What leaves the process waits for the outermost commit: a topic's
publish, a queued command's dispatch, a mail — whose outbox ID [Mailer].Send
returns at once —, a watch's notice, the store's write hooks that wake
workflows and loops, a workflow's OnTransition hooks. Each is checked when
it is made, so a caller's mistake returns to the caller; a rollback drops
them, and a savepoint's rollback its own. A publish, a dispatch, a mail or a
notice whose queue lives on the transaction's database — the one that
keeps the service of its subscription, command, mailer or watch, by a
store's rules — is written in the transaction, just before it commits, a
mail sealed under kit's data-key: a queue that refuses
it fails the transaction, every write undone, and Transact returns the
refusal. Every other one leaves after the commit: one a queue refuses then
is logged and reported, and the commit stands; a process that dies
between the commit and the release loses what was held.

On a database the transaction is the database's own, at its default
isolation. On the data directory and in memory kit keeps its own: it takes
the data's writer turn — one transaction at a time; a write outside any
waits for it, and such writes share the turn among themselves —, its
writes land at once, and an error writes each entity's previous value
back, newest first. It is atomic against an error, not against a crash,
and a reader may see a write before its commit. A store kept in memory by
[InMemory] — a cache — is in no transaction: its writes land and stay.

A command's handler runs in one already ([NoTransaction] opts out), and
so does a workflow's transition.

symbols.name: UID
symbols.doc:
UID identifies an authenticated user. It is what the auth handler returns
and what every endpoint reads with [UserID].

symbols.name: Unauthenticated
symbols.doc: Unauthenticated reports a caller who did not prove who they are (401).

symbols.name: Unavailable
symbols.doc: Unavailable reports a transient failure worth retrying later (503).

symbols.name: Unique
symbols.spelled: func[T any](name string, key func(T) string) StoreOption
symbols.canonical: func[T any](name string, key func(T) string) github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/kit.StoreOption
symbols.doc:
Unique declares a unique index: no two entities may share a key, and a
write that would is refused with a [Conflict] error. An empty key is not
indexed. [Store].Lookup reads it.

	var Accounts = Service.Store("accounts", Account.Key,
		kit.Unique("email", func(a Account) string { return a.Email }))

symbols.name: UserAgent
symbols.doc: UserAgent returns the User-Agent of the request ctx serves, clipped.

symbols.name: UserID
symbols.doc:
UserID returns the authenticated caller of the request ctx serves, and
whether there is one. An in-process [Endpoint].Call carries its caller's
user along.

symbols.name: Violation
symbols.doc:
Violation is one validation rule a request failed: where, which rule, and
why — never the value.

symbols.name: Wake
symbols.doc:
Wake says why a declared loop runs: the reason, the instant, and the
topic that woke it when one did. Wakes that come while it runs, or while
it backs off after a failure, are gathered into one run: Reasons and
Topics say every one of them, and Reason the one that decides the run.

symbols.name: WakeAt
symbols.doc:
WakeAt wakes the loop at the time next returns, asked again after every
run; false means "no deadline for now". It is how a loop sleeps exactly
until its next piece of work — the next reminder due — rather than polling.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: WakeEvery
symbols.doc:
WakeEvery wakes the loop every d.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: WakeOn
symbols.doc:
WakeOn wakes the loop whenever a message is published on topic. It is a
nudge, not a subscription: the loop is not handed the message and wakes
once for a burst — it re-reads the state it works on.

IFACE-OPAQUE: the option is sealed — its method is unexported — so a caller
only hands it to the declaration it configures.

symbols.name: Watch
symbols.doc:
Watch is a subscription fed by stores instead of a topic: its handler is
told of every write kit confirms on a store whose entity holds a field
with its mark. [Service].Watch declares one.

symbols.name: WireCanceled
symbols.doc: WireCanceled is WireCanceled.

symbols.name: WireConflict
symbols.doc: WireConflict is WireConflict.

symbols.name: WireForbidden
symbols.doc: WireForbidden is WireForbidden.

symbols.name: WireInternal
symbols.doc: WireInternal is WireInternal.

symbols.name: WireInvalid
symbols.doc: WireInvalid is WireInvalid.

symbols.name: WireNotFound
symbols.doc: WireNotFound is WireNotFound.

symbols.name: WireRateLimited
symbols.doc: WireRateLimited is WireRateLimited.

symbols.name: WireTimeout
symbols.doc: WireTimeout is WireTimeout.

symbols.name: WireTooLarge
symbols.doc: WireTooLarge is WireTooLarge.

symbols.name: WireUnauth
symbols.doc: WireUnauth is WireUnauth.

symbols.name: WireUnavailable
symbols.doc: WireUnavailable is WireUnavailable.

symbols.name: WireUnsupported
symbols.doc: WireUnsupported is WireUnsupported.

symbols.name: WithUser
symbols.spelled: func[D any](ctx context.Context, uid UID, data D) context.Context
symbols.canonical: func[D any](ctx context.Context, uid github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/kit.UID, data D) context.Context
symbols.doc:
WithUser returns ctx acting as the given user, with data: what a job, a
loop or a test uses to call an [Auth] endpoint in-process on someone's
behalf.

symbols.name: Workflow
symbols.doc:
Workflow is a state machine over the entities of one store: the states an
entity goes through, and the arrows between them. It is declared as data —
which is why the diagram can draw it exactly — and it runs four kinds of
transitions:

  - event transitions ([Workflow].On), fired by code with [Workflow].Fire;
  - timer transitions ([Workflow].After), fired by the workflow's own loop
    once an entity has spent a duration in a state;
  - timer transitions at an instant the entity carries ([Workflow].At) — a
    due date, a deadline — fired by the same loop when it comes;
  - guard transitions ([Workflow].When), fired by the same loop as soon as
    a condition on the entity holds.

The SDK's state-machine engine runs it (statemachine). Its loop never
polls: it keeps an agenda of the transitions due, sleeps until the
earliest, and a write of the store — which may bring one forward — wakes
it. A workflow with nothing due does not run at all. Transitions of one
entity run one at a time, of different entities at once.

The entity's state lives in the entity itself (the state function returns
a pointer to it), so the store stays the single source of truth; the
engine keeps, beside it, when each entity entered its state and the
history of its transitions — in the workflow's file under the data
directory, so a timer keeps counting across a restart.

symbols.name: Written
symbols.doc:
Written is what a watch is told of a write: which store, which record, and
whether it was deleted — never a value. The watch reads the record itself
([RecordsOf]): without its secret members, and journaled.

symbols.name: Disk

fields.name: AppOption
fields.doc: AppOption keeps an app's data in Dir.

fields.name: Dir
fields.doc: Dir is the data directory, removed once the test and its subtests end.

symbols.doc:
Disk is a data directory of a test's own, and the option that runs an app
on it.

symbols.name: Holding
symbols.doc:
Holding returns the files of the data directory that hold one of words,
byte for byte — slash-separated, relative to Dir, sorted —, the secrets
kit keeps there left out: what a test asserts is empty once kit seals
what the words were written into. An empty word matches nothing.

symbols.name: NewDisk
symbols.doc:
NewDisk returns a new data directory for t. The secrets kit makes — its
data-key and its index key, what the product generates — are kept beside
the data, as production keeps them unless KIT_SECRETS says otherwise, so
an app started again on the same Disk opens what the first sealed.

It skips t where the platform keeps no data directory: the SDK's disk
file system is Linux's, macOS's and the BSDs', and refuses Windows.

symbols.name: App
symbols.doc:
App is the name of the app every case runs: a database's URL is read
from STORETEST_<NAME>_URL.

symbols.name: BackendConfig
symbols.spelled: struct{Name string; Options func(t *testing.T, app string) []kit.AppOption}
symbols.canonical: struct{Name string; Options func(t *testing.T, app string) []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/kit.AppOption}

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name names the backend in the subtests.

fields.name: Options
fields.doc:
Options place the stores of the app named app on the backend —
kit.InMemory(), kit.DataDir, a kit.Database whose URL the environment
holds —, once per case. A database is named "database": the suite
gives its calls a minute, as 32 writers of one entity queue on a
server's lock.

symbols.doc:
BackendConfig is where Run runs kit's stores: a name for the subtests and
the options that place the stores there.

symbols.name: CodeRolledBack
symbols.doc:
CodeRolledBack is the code of the error a case returns from a transaction's
function to roll it back — the suite's own, in the framework's range: layer
4, PP 4 this package (ADR 0147 §3). A store never returns it; the case that
returned it expects kit.Transact to hand it back.

symbols.name: Run
symbols.doc: Run runs every case of the suite on b.

symbols.name: AccessAnyUser
symbols.doc:
AccessAnyUser is kit.AnyUser(): any signed-in user may run it — the
operation asks for one.

symbols.name: AccessAnyone
symbols.doc:
AccessAnyone is kit.Anyone(): whoever reaches the route may run the
operation.

symbols.name: Adapter
symbols.doc:
Adapter is a module a connector plugs a product in through: an engine,
imported by the product's main to reach a database, and the only code of
the product that imports its driver.

symbols.name: Analysis
symbols.doc:
Analysis reports the status of static analysis.
It says whether the analyzer ran, how long it took, and the error that
stopped it.

symbols.name: App
symbols.doc:
App identifies the product and the machine that described it.
It names the module, the environment and the build the graph was taken
from.

symbols.name: Architecture
symbols.doc:
Architecture is the product at the two outer levels of the C4 model.

Context (level 1) is the product as one box, the people who use it and the
systems it depends on. Containers (level 2) is what the product is
deployed as: the process, the frontend its browser runs, the volume its
data lives on. Components (level 3) are the nodes, grouped by service; code
(level 4) is each node's [CodeInfo].

kit derives all of it from the declarations — a frontend implies a person
with a browser, a mailer an SMTP relay, a data directory a volume, a
database its own container — so it is exactly as true as the rest of the
graph.

symbols.name: AuthInfo
symbols.doc:
AuthInfo describes the app's authentication handler.
Credentials says what it reads from a request; Endpoints are the ones
behind it.

symbols.name: AuthOptional
symbols.doc:
AuthOptional endpoints run the auth handler when credentials are
present, and serve anonymous callers too.

symbols.name: AuthRequired
symbols.doc:
AuthRequired endpoints run only for an authenticated caller; the others
are answered 401 before the handler runs.

symbols.name: BinaryID
symbols.doc: BinaryID is the ID of a binary.

symbols.name: BinaryInfo
symbols.doc:
BinaryInfo is one executable the product ships: the [Node].Binary of a
[KindBinary] node, naming its roles.

symbols.name: BinaryScope
symbols.doc: BinaryScope prefixes the ID of a binary and of its roles.

symbols.name: BlockCase
symbols.doc: The kinds of [CodeBlock].

symbols.name: BlockDefer
symbols.doc: The kinds of [CodeBlock].

symbols.name: BlockElse
symbols.doc: The kinds of [CodeBlock].

symbols.name: BlockElseIf
symbols.doc: The kinds of [CodeBlock].

symbols.name: BlockFunc
symbols.doc: The kinds of [CodeBlock].

symbols.name: BlockGo
symbols.doc: The kinds of [CodeBlock].

symbols.name: BlockIf
symbols.doc: The kinds of [CodeBlock].

symbols.name: BlockLoop
symbols.doc: The kinds of [CodeBlock].

symbols.name: BlockTransaction
symbols.doc:
BlockTransaction is the function a kit.Transact runs: its steps run in
one transaction, and the effects they make leave at its commit.

symbols.name: BootComponents
symbols.doc: Boot steps, in the order kit takes them.

symbols.name: BootConfig
symbols.doc: Boot steps, in the order kit takes them.

symbols.name: BootData
symbols.doc: Boot steps, in the order kit takes them.

symbols.name: BootDeclarations
symbols.doc: Boot steps, in the order kit takes them.

symbols.name: BootHandler
symbols.doc: Boot steps, in the order kit takes them.

symbols.name: BootMount
symbols.doc: Boot steps, in the order kit takes them.

symbols.name: BootRoutes
symbols.doc: Boot steps, in the order kit takes them.

symbols.name: BootServing
symbols.doc: Boot steps, in the order kit takes them.

symbols.name: BootStep
symbols.doc:
BootStep is one step of the start, as it ran.
It carries when it began, how long it took and, when it failed, its error.

symbols.name: Build
symbols.doc:
Build is what a binary was built from, at its three levels.
Its three levels are the Go toolchain, the main module and the modules it
depends on.

symbols.name: CLIInfo
symbols.doc:
CLIInfo is a short command-line command: the [Node].CLI of a [KindCLI]
node, the words that run it.

symbols.name: Census
symbols.doc:
Census is a workflow's population per state.
It counts the instances in each state when the census was taken.

symbols.name: ClassPersonal
symbols.doc:
ClassPersonal holds data about an identifiable person: a name, an
address, a message a person wrote.

symbols.name: ClassPublic
symbols.doc:
ClassPublic holds nothing personal and nothing secret: the question
was asked.

symbols.name: ClassSecret
symbols.doc: ClassSecret holds a credential: a password's hash, a token's digest.

symbols.name: ClassSpecial
symbols.doc:
ClassSpecial holds the special categories of GDPR art. 9(1), or
criminal convictions (art. 10).

symbols.name: CodeBlock
symbols.doc:
CodeBlock is a block of a function that decides whether, or how many
times, the steps under it run.

symbols.name: CodeEffect
symbols.doc:
CodeEffect is one call on a building block, inside a function.
It names the node it reaches and the edge kind that call draws.

symbols.name: CodeFunc
symbols.doc:
CodeFunc is one function of the module a node's code reaches.
Its steps are listed in the order they run, under the blocks that guard
them.

symbols.name: CodeInfo
symbols.doc:
CodeInfo is the code a node runs, as the static analysis read it: the
fourth and innermost level of the C4 model. The entry is the function the
node runs — an endpoint's handler, a subscription's, a loop's — and Funcs
are the functions of the module it reaches, each with what it calls and
what it does to other nodes.

symbols.name: CodeInvalidID
symbols.doc: CodeInvalidID identifies an ID the grammar of [IDPattern] does not match.

symbols.name: CodeStep
symbols.doc:
CodeStep is one thing a function does: a call to another function of the
module, a call on a building block, or a call into the SDK — under the
innermost block that guards it.

symbols.name: CodeUse
symbols.doc:
CodeUse is one SDK function a node's code calls.
Sites are where the node's code calls it, so a reader sees what it leans
on.

symbols.name: CommandInfo
symbols.doc:
CommandInfo describes a command: an operation that changes something.
It carries its input and result schemas, its handler, its queue and who may
dispatch it.

symbols.name: CompareSource
symbols.doc: CompareSource orders sources by root, file, then line.

symbols.name: Component
symbols.doc:
Component is one lifecycle component: brought up in order, taken down in
reverse.

symbols.name: ComponentDown
symbols.doc: Component states.

symbols.name: ComponentFailed
symbols.doc: Component states.

symbols.name: ComponentPending
symbols.doc: Component states.

symbols.name: ComponentStarting
symbols.doc: Component states.

symbols.name: ComponentStopping
symbols.doc: Component states.

symbols.name: ComponentUp
symbols.doc: Component states.

symbols.name: Connector
symbols.doc:
Connector is something a product plugs into, as the product declares it:
how it is reached, what it reaches out to, where it keeps its data. The
Studio shows a connector's pages and widgets only when the product has
one: a command-line tool has no requests to list, a service without a
mailer no mailbox.

A connector says what the code declares, never what an environment
supplies. The relay a mailer delivers through, the directory a store
writes to, the address kit listens on are facts of the running
environment — [MailerInfo], [StoreInfo], the [Architecture] and [Runtime]
carry those. So a connector is a pure function of the nodes
([ConnectorsOf]), and never moves a graph's revision.

symbols.name: ConnectorCatalog
symbols.doc:
ConnectorCatalog is every connector kit ships, sorted by ID: what a
product may plug into.

symbols.name: ConnectorData
symbols.doc: ConnectorData is where it keeps its data: stores, databases.

symbols.name: ConnectorDatabase
symbols.doc:
ConnectorDatabase is brought by a store a database keeps (ADR 0004):
kit.Database declares the database, an engine module reaches it.

symbols.name: ConnectorHTTP
symbols.doc: The connectors kit ships.

symbols.name: ConnectorInfo
symbols.doc:
ConnectorInfo is a connector kit can plug a product into, whether the
product uses it or not: what it is, and the building blocks that bring it.

symbols.name: ConnectorKind
symbols.doc: ConnectorKind groups connectors by what they are for.

symbols.name: ConnectorMail
symbols.doc: The connectors kit ships.

symbols.name: ConnectorMessaging
symbols.doc: ConnectorMessaging is what it sends and receives: mail, queues.

symbols.name: ConnectorQueue
symbols.doc: The connectors kit ships.

symbols.name: ConnectorStore
symbols.doc: The connectors kit ships.

symbols.name: ConnectorTransport
symbols.doc: ConnectorTransport is how the product is reached: HTTP.

symbols.name: ConnectorsOf
symbols.doc:
ConnectorsOf derives the connectors a product uses from its nodes: an
endpoint, a frontend or an auth handler means HTTP, a mailer mail, a store
stores — and a database when one keeps it —, a topic, a subscription or
a queued command queues. Sorted by ID.

symbols.name: Container
symbols.doc:
Container is one runnable or storage unit of the product.
Its ID starts with "container:"; Nodes are the nodes that live in it.

symbols.name: ContainerDatabase
symbols.doc:
ContainerDatabase is a database the app declares (kit.Database):
"container:database:<name>", drawn as a cylinder.

symbols.name: ContainerMemory
symbols.doc: Container kinds.

symbols.name: ContainerProcess
symbols.doc: Container kinds.

symbols.name: ContainerSPA
symbols.doc: Container kinds.

symbols.name: ContainerVolume
symbols.doc: Container kinds.

symbols.name: ContractPattern
symbols.doc:
ContractPattern is the versioned contract an [EdgeContracts] edge
carries: "render/v1".

symbols.name: Database
symbols.doc:
Database is one database the app declares (kit.Database), as the running
process found it. Its URL is never shown: where it was found, the engine,
the address and the TLS mode are.

symbols.name: DatabaseClosed
symbols.doc: DatabaseClosed: not opened yet, or closed by the stop.

symbols.name: DatabaseFailed
symbols.doc: DatabaseFailed: the start could not open it, migrate it or reach it.

symbols.name: DatabaseMemory
symbols.doc:
DatabaseMemory: the app keeps its data in memory (kit.InMemory):
nothing is opened, no URL is read.

symbols.name: DatabaseOpen
symbols.doc:
DatabaseOpen: the pool is open, its migrations ran, it answered its
check at start.

symbols.name: DatabaseUnset
symbols.doc:
DatabaseUnset: no URL, in dev. Its stores stay in the data directory
and nothing is opened.

symbols.name: DevBuild
symbols.doc:
DevBuild is one build of `kit dev`: when, how long, and why.
It lets the Studio say what changed and how long the reload took.

symbols.name: Diagnostic
symbols.doc:
Diagnostic is a problem found while building the graph.
It names the node or the file it is about, and how serious it is.

symbols.name: Edge
symbols.doc:
Edge is one relation, with the evidence for it.
Declared, Static and Observed say whether construction, the code or the
runtime knows it.

symbols.name: EdgeAsks
symbols.doc:
EdgeAsks targets a query: the source asks it. From an endpoint that
exposes the query, or from a port bound to it, it is declared.

symbols.name: EdgeCalls
symbols.doc:
EdgeCalls targets an endpoint or a port. From a port, it is the port's
binding — what the port calls — and it is declared.

symbols.name: EdgeContracts
symbols.doc:
EdgeContracts goes from one process role to another it talks to —
through a socket, a pipe, a command line —, and names the versioned
contract they share in [Edge].Contract. It is the only edge between two
roles (D22). Declared.

symbols.name: EdgeDelivers
symbols.doc:
EdgeDelivers goes from a topic to each of its subscriptions, and from a
store to each watch it feeds (ADR 0008). Declared.

symbols.name: EdgeDispatches
symbols.doc:
EdgeDispatches targets a command: the source dispatches it. From an
endpoint that exposes the command, or from a port bound to it, it is
declared.

symbols.name: EdgeID
symbols.spelled: func(from string, kind EdgeKind, to string, label string) string
symbols.canonical: func(from string, kind github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/model.EdgeKind, to string, label string) string
symbols.doc:
EdgeID builds the ID of an edge. The label is part of the identity: two
transitions of one workflow fired from one endpoint are two edges.

symbols.name: EdgeImports
symbols.doc:
EdgeImports goes from a component to a library it may import (D19).
Declared.

symbols.name: EdgeKind
symbols.doc:
EdgeKind says how two nodes relate.
It is a wire format — the graph's JSON and the Studio's TypeScript unions
carry these names —, so it stays a string.

symbols.name: EdgePersists
symbols.doc: EdgePersists goes from a workflow to the store it lives in. Declared.

symbols.name: EdgePublishes
symbols.doc: EdgePublishes targets a topic.

symbols.name: EdgeReads
symbols.doc: EdgeReads targets a store the source reads from.

symbols.name: EdgeRenders
symbols.doc: EdgeRenders goes from a presentation to what it renders. Declared.

symbols.name: EdgeRuns
symbols.doc:
EdgeRuns goes from a role to what it runs: a CLI command, a listener,
an endpoint's server, a loop. Declared.

symbols.name: EdgeSends
symbols.doc: EdgeSends targets a mailer: the source puts a message in its outbox.

symbols.name: EdgeTransitions
symbols.doc: EdgeTransitions targets a workflow; Label carries the event.

symbols.name: EdgeUses
symbols.doc: EdgeUses targets a secret whose value or keys the source uses.

symbols.name: EdgeWakes
symbols.doc: EdgeWakes goes from a topic to a declared loop it wakes. Declared.

symbols.name: EdgeWrites
symbols.doc: EdgeWrites targets a store the source writes to.

symbols.name: Edit
symbols.doc:
Edit is one change between two versions of a record, in RFC 6902's
words: an add, a remove or a replace at a JSON pointer.

symbols.name: EndpointInfo
symbols.doc:
EndpointInfo describes an HTTP endpoint, or the implementation of a port.
It carries the method and path, the request and response schemas, and its
auth.

symbols.name: EngineMySQL
symbols.doc:
The engines a database runs on (ADR 0004): one module each in kit's
repository, the only code that imports its driver.

symbols.name: EnginePostgres
symbols.doc:
The engines a database runs on (ADR 0004): one module each in kit's
repository, the only code that imports its driver.

symbols.name: EngineSQLite
symbols.doc:
The engines a database runs on (ADR 0004): one module each in kit's
repository, the only code that imports its driver.

symbols.name: Erasure
symbols.doc:
Erasure is what kit.Erase did, store by store.
Stores lists, store by store, what the erasure did there.

symbols.name: Event
symbols.doc:
Event is one live event. Exactly one of the payload fields matching Type is
set.

symbols.name: EventCensus
symbols.doc: EventCensus reports a workflow's population per state.

symbols.name: EventGraph
symbols.doc: EventGraph reports that the graph structure changed.

symbols.name: EventHello
symbols.doc: EventHello opens every stream and carries the graph revision.

symbols.name: EventLifecycle
symbols.doc:
EventLifecycle reports a lifecycle component moving, or the process
changing phase.

symbols.name: EventLog
symbols.doc: EventLog reports a log record written by product code, in dev.

symbols.name: EventLoop
symbols.doc: EventLoop reports a loop run.

symbols.name: EventMail
symbols.doc: EventMail reports a mail entering the outbox or changing status.

symbols.name: EventSpan
symbols.doc: EventSpan reports one unit of work that finished on a node.

symbols.name: EventTransition
symbols.doc: EventTransition reports a workflow instance changing state.

symbols.name: EventType
symbols.doc:
EventType names the kind of a live event.
It is a wire format — the graph's JSON and the Studio's TypeScript unions
carry these names —, so it stays a string.

symbols.name: ExportedVersions
symbols.doc: ExportedVersions are the versions of one exported record.

symbols.name: ExposePrivate
symbols.doc:
ExposePrivate endpoints have no route: the implementation of a port
(Service.Implement), reached in process through its port. A graph kit
made before its operations were internal by default also marks so an
endpoint it kept off the listener.

symbols.name: ExposePublic
symbols.doc: ExposePublic endpoints are routed on the product's HTTP listener.

symbols.name: ExternalID
symbols.doc: ExternalID is the id of the node standing for the outside world.

symbols.name: Field
symbols.doc:
Field is one member of an object schema.
It carries the JSON name, the schema of its value and the classes of its
data.

symbols.name: File
symbols.doc:
File is one file a graph points at: its path, relative to its root — the
product's module, or the Go module [Source].GoModule names.

symbols.name: FlameNode
symbols.doc:
FlameNode is one frame of a flame graph.
Its children are the frames it called; its value is the samples under it.

symbols.name: Former
symbols.doc:
Former is one former value of a field that keeps its history: what it
was, until when, and who replaced it.

symbols.name: FrontendInfo
symbols.doc:
FrontendInfo describes static assets served by the product.
It carries the path the assets are served under and where they are read
from.

symbols.name: FuncCost
symbols.doc:
FuncCost is what one function cost.
It carries the flat and cumulative samples of the function and where it
lives.

symbols.name: GapPurpose
symbols.doc: The gaps a register lists for a store that keeps personal data.

symbols.name: GapRetention
symbols.doc: The gaps a register lists for a store that keeps personal data.

symbols.name: GapSubject
symbols.doc: The gaps a register lists for a store that keeps personal data.

symbols.name: GoroutineGroup
symbols.doc:
GoroutineGroup is goroutines doing the same thing.
They share one stack; Count says how many run it.

symbols.name: Goroutines
symbols.doc:
Goroutines is every goroutine of the process, grouped by what it runs.
Each group names the node its stack runs in, when one does.

symbols.name: Graph
symbols.doc:
Graph is the whole product.
It is the JSON document the runtime serves and the analyzer writes; Version
names its shape.

symbols.name: HTTPServer
symbols.doc:
HTTPServer is the product's HTTP server, and whose loop serves it.
Its address is the one it listens on; its loop is the node that runs it.

symbols.name: HeldUntil
symbols.doc:
HeldUntil is the hold a store declares on each of its records, until an
instant the record carries.

symbols.name: Hold
symbols.doc:
Hold is one record a legal hold keeps. It carries references only: never
the record's key, its subject's identity, or the hold's reason, which kit
keeps apart.

symbols.name: ID
symbols.doc:
ID is a node's identity, parsed: the one grammar of [IDPattern]. Its
String is the ID it was parsed from.

symbols.name: IDPattern
symbols.doc:
IDPattern is the whole grammar as one regular expression, anchored —
the one the design files' JSON Schema publishes for an ID. Only an
endpoint may be named by its route.

symbols.name: IndexInfo
symbols.doc:
IndexInfo is one secondary index of a store.
Its name is unique in the store; Unique says whether two records may share
a key.

symbols.name: Instance
symbols.doc:
Instance is one entity's journey through a workflow.
It carries the entity's key, its current state and the steps that brought
it there.

symbols.name: InvalidID

code.public: The node identifier is not valid

symbols.doc:
InvalidID is returned by [ParseID] for a string the ID grammar does not
match. Its "part" field names what failed — the kind, the service name, the
node name —, never the input.

symbols.name: IsEngine
symbols.doc: IsEngine reports whether backend names an engine a database runs on.

symbols.name: JobInfo
symbols.doc:
JobInfo describes a scheduled job.
It carries the fixed interval or the cron expression that schedules it.

symbols.name: JournalCheck
symbols.doc:
JournalCheck is what verifying the journal's chain found.
A broken chain names the first entry whose hash does not follow.

symbols.name: JournalDelete
symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.name: JournalEntry
symbols.doc:
JournalEntry is one operation of the privacy journal: what was done,
where, by whom and when, with references only — never an identity, a
value or a key. Each entry is chained to the previous one by SHA-256.

symbols.name: JournalErase
symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.name: JournalEraseFields
symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.name: JournalExport
symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.name: JournalHold
symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.name: JournalList
symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.name: JournalRead
symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.name: JournalRelease
symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.name: JournalShred
symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.name: KindAuth
symbols.doc:
KindAuth is the app's authentication handler: it turns a request's
credentials into a user, in front of every endpoint that asks for one.

symbols.name: KindBinary
symbols.doc:
KindBinary is one executable the product ships. It holds process
roles; its ID is "binary:<name>".

symbols.name: KindCLI
symbols.doc:
KindCLI is a short command-line command: it parses its arguments,
runs once and exits with a typed status.

symbols.name: KindCommand
symbols.doc:
KindCommand is an operation that changes something: a typed input, a
typed result, one handler, the pipeline of its kind. It is dispatched,
on its caller's goroutine or through its own queue.

symbols.name: KindEndpoint
symbols.doc: KindEndpoint is an HTTP endpoint with typed request and response.

symbols.name: KindExternal
symbols.doc: KindExternal stands for everything outside the product.

symbols.name: KindFrontend
symbols.doc: KindFrontend is static assets served by the product.

symbols.name: KindJob
symbols.doc: KindJob is scheduled work: a fixed interval or a cron expression.

symbols.name: KindLibrary
symbols.doc:
KindLibrary is a package shared between components, declared so the
components that use it are allowed to import it. Its ID is
"library:<name>".

symbols.name: KindListener
symbols.doc:
KindListener accepts connections that are not HTTP: a private Unix
socket, a named pipe. It is an inbound port like an endpoint.

symbols.name: KindLoop
symbols.doc:
KindLoop is a long-running loop of the daemon: declared (kit owns the
wait, the product the work) or hand-written (a goroutine kit supervises).

symbols.name: KindMailer
symbols.doc:
KindMailer is outbound mail: a durable outbox, and the transport that
empties it — SMTP, or the capture of dev and tests.

symbols.name: KindPort
symbols.doc:
KindPort is an operation a service needs and does not implement: a
typed request, a typed response, a name. What it calls — another
service's endpoint, the app's binding, its own fallback — is decided
when the app starts, and drawn as a declared edge from the port.

symbols.name: KindPresentation
symbols.doc:
KindPresentation turns a service's results into what a reader sees:
a rendered line, a page, a report.

symbols.name: KindQuery
symbols.doc:
KindQuery is an operation that reads and changes nothing: a typed
input, a typed result, one handler. It is asked.

symbols.name: KindRole
symbols.doc:
KindRole is one process role of a binary — "statusline" and
"statusline daemon" are two roles of one binary. Its root package is
generated wiring; two roles talk through their contract only. Its ID
is "binary:<binary>/role/<name>".

symbols.name: KindSecret
symbols.doc:
KindSecret is a secret the product declares: provided by the operator,
or generated by kit and rotated on a schedule. Its value is never in a
graph.

symbols.name: KindService
symbols.doc: KindService groups the nodes of one bounded context.

symbols.name: KindStore
symbols.doc: KindStore is a typed, keyed collection of entities.

symbols.name: KindSubscription
symbols.doc: KindSubscription consumes one topic.

symbols.name: KindTopic
symbols.doc: KindTopic is an asynchronous, at-least-once message channel.

symbols.name: KindWorkflow
symbols.doc: KindWorkflow is a state machine over the entities of one store.

symbols.name: LibraryID
symbols.doc: LibraryID is the ID of a library.

symbols.name: LibraryInfo
symbols.doc:
LibraryInfo is a package shared between components (D19): the
[Node].Library of a [KindLibrary] node.

symbols.name: LibraryScope
symbols.doc: LibraryScope prefixes the ID of a library.

symbols.name: Link
symbols.doc:
Link is a relationship between two elements of the architecture. The
process's link to a database, "Reads and writes", carries the database
connector, and the store connector once stores live on it.

symbols.name: ListenerInfo
symbols.doc:
ListenerInfo is a listener that is not HTTP: the [Node].Listener of a
[KindListener] node — its network, its contract, who may connect.

symbols.name: LogRecord
symbols.doc:
LogRecord is one log record written by product code through kit.Log, kept
in dev so the Studio can show a request's logs beside its spans.

symbols.name: Loop
symbols.doc:
Loop is one recurring piece of the daemon's internal loop: a job, a
workflow's timer sweep, a subscription's consumer, the HTTP accept loop, a
declared or hand-written loop.

symbols.name: LoopConsumer
symbols.doc: Loop kinds.

symbols.name: LoopDeclared
symbols.doc:
LoopDeclared is Service.Loop: kit owns the wait — the wake sources are
data, so the diagram draws them — and the product owns the work.

symbols.name: LoopGoroutine
symbols.doc:
LoopGoroutine is Service.Go: the product wrote the whole loop; kit
starts it, stops it, restarts it after a failure, and reads its select
statements to draw what it waits on.

symbols.name: LoopHTTP
symbols.doc: Loop kinds.

symbols.name: LoopInfo
symbols.doc:
LoopInfo describes a loop node.
Style says whether it is declared (kit owns the wait) or hand-written.

symbols.name: LoopJob
symbols.doc: Loop kinds.

symbols.name: LoopRestarting
symbols.doc: Loop states.

symbols.name: LoopRetention
symbols.doc: Loop kinds.

symbols.name: LoopRotation
symbols.doc: Loop kinds.

symbols.name: LoopRoutine
symbols.doc: Loop kinds.

symbols.name: LoopRunning
symbols.doc: Loop states.

symbols.name: LoopScheduler
symbols.doc: Loop kinds.

symbols.name: LoopStopped
symbols.doc: Loop states.

symbols.name: LoopTimer
symbols.doc: Loop kinds.

symbols.name: LoopWaiting
symbols.doc: Loop states.

symbols.name: LoopWake
symbols.doc: Loop kinds.

symbols.name: MailDead
symbols.doc: Mail statuses.

symbols.name: MailMessage
symbols.doc:
MailMessage is a whole captured mail, for the Studio's mailbox.
It is kept by the capture transport of dev and tests only, never in
production.

symbols.name: MailQueued
symbols.doc: Mail statuses.

symbols.name: MailRetrying
symbols.doc: Mail statuses.

symbols.name: MailSent
symbols.doc: Mail statuses.

symbols.name: MailSummary
symbols.doc:
MailSummary is the name [MailMessage] embeds its summary under: the field
a caller sets and reads is MailMessage.MailSummary, its JSON members
promoted beside the body's.

symbols.name: MailerInfo
symbols.doc:
MailerInfo describes outbound mail.
It carries the transport that empties the outbox and the outbox's counters.

symbols.name: MaxTableLen
symbols.doc:
MaxTableLen is the longest table name a store on a database takes, in
bytes: the SDK's document store over SQL keeps its index rows in the table
named after it with "___ix", within PostgreSQL's 63.

symbols.name: MeasureHolds
symbols.doc: MeasureHolds: a legal hold stops erasure and deletion.

symbols.name: MeasureJournal
symbols.doc:
MeasureJournal: every export, erasure, deletion and hold is journaled,
each entry chained to the previous one by SHA-256.

symbols.name: MeasureNotSealed
symbols.doc:
MeasureNotSealed: the store's classified members are in clear: it is
kept in memory, where nothing is at rest, or its members are plain.

symbols.name: MeasureRedacted
symbols.doc:
MeasureRedacted: the Studio, the spans and the logs never show a
personal, special or secret value.

symbols.name: MeasureSealed
symbols.doc:
MeasureSealed: its classified members are sealed at rest, AES-256-GCM
under per-subject data keys a person's erasure destroys (ADR 0006 §4).

symbols.name: Mechanic
symbols.doc:
Mechanic is a generic building block, backed by an SDK package, that a node
composes. The catalog lists every mechanic kit offers; an endpoint's
pipeline lists the ones it uses.

symbols.name: Merge
symbols.doc:
Merge enriches a graph with what another description of the same product
knows. base is authoritative on which nodes exist — a runtime graph describes
what the process actually serves —, on the modules it mounts, on what each
of its ports calls and on which stores feed each of its watches: the app
chose them when it started, where the analysis only reads the same rules
over the whole module. extra, typically
the static analysis, contributes documentation, handler ranges — an
authorization function's too —, transition callers and the edges it
found. Nodes only extra knows about are dropped: code that is compiled but
not mounted in this app is not part of this product — save a node of a
module's service the base mounts, which a package the binary does not link
declares: a warning says so.

symbols.name: Mermaid
symbols.doc:
Mermaid renders the architecture of a graph as a Mermaid flowchart: one
subgraph per service — a module's inside the module's own, ADR 0008 —, one
arrow per edge. GitHub renders it in Markdown, which makes a product's
README carry its own, always regenerable, diagram.

Each kind has its shape: an endpoint a box (marked "auth" when it asks for
a user; an implementation of a port by its name), a store a cylinder, a
topic a flag, a subscription a parallelogram (a watch, ADR 0008, marked
with the mark it watches — its stores' arrows say where from), a
workflow a hexagon, a job a
stadium, the auth handler a trapezoid — a gate —, a mailer a subroutine
box, a declared loop a circle, a hand-written loop a double circle, a
port an inverted trapezoid — a socket, UML's required interface —, a
command a parallelogram leaning back — a subscription's leans forward —,
marked "queued" when it waits in its queue, and a query a rhombus, a
question. An arrow is solid when it exists by construction or was
observed, dotted when only the code says so — or when it is a port's
binding to its own fallback, the default the app may replace, as the
Studio draws it.

symbols.name: Migration
symbols.doc:
Migration is one versioned migration.
Its Version orders it among the others; Name says what it does.

symbols.name: MigrationSet
symbols.doc:
MigrationSet is one set of migrations on a database — kit's own, the
product's (kit.Migrations), a module's — with its own version table, and
so its own lock.

symbols.name: Mock
symbols.doc:
Mock is the replacement a test gave the app ([MockReplace]).
It is set by a test only; the Studio shows it and never sets one (D13).

symbols.name: MockReplace
symbols.doc:
MockReplace is the one mode a [Mock] has: a test's kit.Replace, a typed
function run in place of an operation's handler — or of what a port calls —
while the rest of its pipeline still runs. The Studio sets none (D13): it
shows the application, it does not act on it, so the respond, fail and
delay modes of the platform's kit have no representation here.

symbols.name: ModeQueued
symbols.doc:
ModeQueued is sent to the background (kit.Queued): Dispatch returns
once the command's own queue accepted it, and a consumer handles it,
retried and dead-lettered.

symbols.name: ModeSync
symbols.doc:
ModeSync is handled on its caller's goroutine: Dispatch returns the
handler's result.

symbols.name: Module
symbols.doc:
Module is a module the app mounts: a Go module's services, released and
mounted together like a bundle (ADR 0008). Everything a module declares is
qualified with its name: its services are "<module>.<service>" — the one
named like the module is "<module>" —, so its nodes are
"<module>.<service>/<kind>/<name>" and carry [Node].Module.

symbols.name: ModulePrefix
symbols.doc: ModulePrefix is a module's default mount prefix: "/<name>/".

symbols.name: ModuleVersion
symbols.doc:
ModuleVersion identifies one module of a build.
Local and Modified say when the code that ran is not the published version.

symbols.name: NamePattern
symbols.doc: NamePattern is a node's name within its service and kind.

symbols.name: NetworkLocal
symbols.doc:
NetworkLocal is NetworkUnix where there is one, NetworkPipe on
Windows: what a product declares when it does not care which.

symbols.name: NetworkPipe
symbols.doc: NetworkPipe is a Windows named pipe, its DACL granting its owner only.

symbols.name: NetworkUnix
symbols.doc: NetworkUnix is a Unix-domain socket, private to its owner.

symbols.name: Node
symbols.doc:
Node is one building block.
Its ID is its identity; exactly one of the kind-specific fields matching
Kind is set.

symbols.name: NodeCost
symbols.doc:
NodeCost is what one node cost.
It is the share of the profile's samples spent in the node's code.

symbols.name: NodeID
symbols.spelled: func(service string, kind NodeKind, name string) string
symbols.canonical: func(service string, kind github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/model.NodeKind, name string) string
symbols.doc:
NodeID builds the ID of a node declared in a service. A service's own ID is
its name.

symbols.name: NodeKind
symbols.doc:
