NodeKind is the closed set of building blocks a kit product is made of.
It is a wire format — the graph's JSON and the Studio's TypeScript unions
carry these names —, so it stays a string.

symbols.name: OpAsk
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpAuth
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpCLI
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpCall
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpConnect
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpDeliver
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpDeliverMail
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpDispatch
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpHandle
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpPublish
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpRead
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpRequest
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpRun
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpSecret
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpSend
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpTransaction
symbols.doc:
OpTransaction is a unit of work (kit.Transact, a command's, a
workflow's transition): its attrs say the database it belongs to —
"database", and "backend" as a store says it —, its "outcome", the
effects it held ("effects"), and "savepoint" for one nested in
another.

symbols.name: OpTransition
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OpWrite
symbols.doc: Span operations.

symbols.name: OutcomeCommit
symbols.doc: OutcomeCommit is a transaction that committed: its effects left.

symbols.name: OutcomeRollback
symbols.doc:
OutcomeRollback is a transaction whose writes were undone: its effects
were dropped.

symbols.name: ParseID
symbols.doc:
ParseID reads an ID. It refuses anything [IDPattern] does not match, with
[InvalidID]; the refusal never quotes the input, which may be anything a
caller sent.

symbols.name: PasswordPolicy
symbols.doc:
PasswordPolicy is the policy of one secret field that holds a password's
hash (Store.Passwords).

symbols.name: Payload
symbols.doc:
Payload is the request and the response of a span, as JSON, in dev only.
Every member whose name says it is a secret — password, token, secret,
authorization, cookie… — or whose Go field is tagged kit:"secret" is
replaced by "[redacted]", and each side is cut at 8 KiB.

symbols.name: Permission
symbols.doc:
Permission is what a caller needs to dispatch a command or to ask a
query: that the app's policy lets it do Action to Resource (Allow).

symbols.name: Person
symbols.doc:
Person is a human user of the product.
It is drawn at the edge of the C4 context view, outside every container.

symbols.name: PersonalData
symbols.doc:
PersonalData is a person's data as kit.Export gives it (GDPR art. 15 and
20): their records, store by store, with what art. 15(1) asks beside them.

symbols.name: PhaseChange
symbols.doc:
PhaseChange is one step of the daemon's life.
It carries the phase entered, when it was entered, and why.

symbols.name: PhaseDraining
symbols.doc: Process phases, in the order a process goes through them.

symbols.name: PhaseFailed
symbols.doc: Process phases, in the order a process goes through them.

symbols.name: PhaseServing
symbols.doc: Process phases, in the order a process goes through them.

symbols.name: PhaseStarting
symbols.doc: Process phases, in the order a process goes through them.

symbols.name: PhaseStopped
symbols.doc: Process phases, in the order a process goes through them.

symbols.name: Pool
symbols.doc:
Pool is a database's connection pool, as database/sql counts it.
It is sampled when the runtime state is read; its counters never move a
revision.

symbols.name: Port
symbols.doc:
Port is an address a process listens on.
Owner is the container that listens on it; Serves names what is reached
through it.

symbols.name: PortInfo
symbols.doc:
PortInfo describes a port: an operation a service needs and another
implements.

symbols.name: PortOwnerKit
symbols.doc:
PortOwnerKit is kit's own listener: the health probes, the Studio in
dev, and the product's HTTP when it declares any.

symbols.name: PresentationInfo
symbols.doc:
PresentationInfo is what turns results into what a reader sees: the
[Node].Presentation of a [KindPresentation] node.

symbols.name: Privacy
symbols.doc:
Privacy is what a running app says of the personal data it keeps.
It is the Privacy page's data: the register, the holds and the journal's
state.

symbols.name: Process
symbols.doc:
Process is the Go process a product runs in.
It carries the runtime's figures — goroutines, heap, GC, CPU — taken at At.

symbols.name: ProductRetention
symbols.doc:
ProductRetention is a retention the product keeps itself, as it says
it.

symbols.name: Profile
symbols.doc:
Profile is a pprof profile of the running product, folded onto its graph:
every sample is attributed to the node whose code was running — through
the pprof label kit puts on every handler, subscription, job and loop run,
or, for the heap, which carries no label, through the node's code functions
on the sample's stack.

symbols.name: ProfileCLI
symbols.doc:
ProfileCLI parses its arguments, runs once and exits with a typed
status. It starts no listener and no loop outlives it.

symbols.name: ProfileCPU
symbols.doc: Profile kinds.

symbols.name: ProfileDaemon
symbols.doc:
ProfileDaemon runs until it is stopped, or until it has been idle for
its declared time, and serves no HTTP: it answers on its listeners —
a private socket, a pipe — and runs its loops.

symbols.name: ProfileHeap
symbols.doc: Profile kinds.

symbols.name: ProfileServer
symbols.doc:
ProfileServer serves HTTP until it is stopped: the platform's kit
product, and the only profile that opens a TCP listener.

symbols.name: ProvenanceKit
symbols.doc:
ProvenanceKit loops are written by kit for a declaration: a workflow's
sweep, a declared loop's wake cycle.

symbols.name: ProvenanceLibrary
symbols.doc:
ProvenanceLibrary loops are written by a library: net/http's accept
loop, the SDK scheduler, the SDK queue consumer.

symbols.name: ProvenanceProduct
symbols.doc: ProvenanceProduct loops are written by hand in the product: Service.Go.

symbols.name: QualifiedService
symbols.doc:
QualifiedService is the name a module gives a service it lists: the
module's own name for the service named like it, "<module>.<service>"
otherwise. The runtime and the analyzer both qualify with it.

symbols.name: QueryInfo
symbols.doc:
QueryInfo describes a query: an operation that reads and changes
nothing.

symbols.name: RecordFormer
symbols.doc:
RecordFormer is the former values of one exported record's fields.
A personal or special field's former values are redacted, never exported in
clear.

symbols.name: RecordHistory
symbols.doc:
RecordHistory is what kit remembers of one record, as the Studio's data
view shows it (GET /_kit/api/former): each field's former values, newest
first, by the field's JSON pointer — a secret field's without their
values, a personal or special one's redacted.

symbols.name: RecordVersion
symbols.doc:
RecordVersion is one version of a record whose store keeps revisions
(ADR 0007 §3): its number, when the write that made it ran, who made
it and which command, and the record as it was.

symbols.name: RecordVersions
symbols.doc:
RecordVersions is a record's versions as the Studio's data view shows
them (GET /_kit/api/revisions), and what changed between two.

symbols.name: Register
symbols.doc:
Register is the record of processing of GDPR art. 30(1), as far as the
code knows it.

symbols.name: RegisterStore
symbols.doc:
RegisterStore is one store's line in the register.
It names the classes the store keeps, their purposes and their retention.

symbols.name: Retention
symbols.doc:
Retention is when kit erases or deletes a record: after a delay counted
from an instant the record carries (After or Setting, and Since), or at an
instant a function gives (At).

symbols.name: RetentionDryRun
symbols.doc:
RetentionDryRun journals what the retention would do and changes
nothing: how a new retention is deployed over old data.

symbols.name: RetentionOff
symbols.doc: RetentionOff runs no retention, warned of at every start outside dev.

symbols.name: RetentionOn
symbols.doc: RetentionOn erases and deletes what is due: the default.

symbols.name: RoleID
symbols.doc: RoleID is the ID of one process role of a binary.

symbols.name: RoleInbound
symbols.doc: The roles of a connector, against the process boundary.

symbols.name: RoleInfo
symbols.doc:
RoleInfo is one process role of a binary: the [Node].Role of a
[KindRole] node — its profile, arguments, singleton and idle stop.

symbols.name: RoleOutbound
symbols.doc: The roles of a connector, against the process boundary.

symbols.name: RoleStorage
symbols.doc: The roles of a connector, against the process boundary.

symbols.name: RoutePattern
symbols.doc:
RoutePattern is the name of an endpoint declared without one: its
route, "GET /tasks/{id}".

symbols.name: Runtime
symbols.doc:
Runtime is what a running process says about itself: the daemon's own state
and its internal loop.

symbols.name: Schema
symbols.doc:
Schema describes a Go type as it appears on the wire.
It is a JSON-Schema-like shape: a kind, its fields or elements, and its Go
type.

symbols.name: SealedPlaceholder
symbols.doc:
SealedPlaceholder is what the Studio receives in place of a value kit
keeps sealed at rest — a record's member in the data browser, a former
value —: never the value, nor its box (ADR 0006 §9). A value it opens and
may not show is "[redacted]".

symbols.name: SecretFromEnv
symbols.doc:
SecretFromEnv is the environment: the variable, or the file its _FILE
form names.

symbols.name: SecretFromFile
symbols.doc:
SecretFromFile is kit's encrypted file store: KIT_SECRETS=file:<dir>,
or .kit/secrets/dev in dev.

symbols.name: SecretFromMemory
symbols.doc:
SecretFromMemory is a store in the process's memory: a test, or
KIT_SECRETS=memory. A generated secret is made again at every start.

symbols.name: SecretFromStore
symbols.doc: SecretFromStore is a store the product's code gave kit.

symbols.name: SecretGenerated
symbols.doc:
SecretGenerated is made by kit and rotated on a schedule: a signing or
sealing key.

symbols.name: SecretInfo
symbols.doc:
SecretInfo describes a declared secret: how it is made, where it lives,
its versions — never its value.

symbols.name: SecretProvided
symbols.doc: SecretProvided is given by the operator: an SMTP URL, an API token.

symbols.name: SegmentPattern
symbols.doc: SegmentPattern is a service, module, binary, role or library name.

symbols.name: SelectCase
symbols.doc:
SelectCase is one case of a select statement in a hand-written loop.
The analyzer reads it from the loop's body; Kind says what the case waits
on.

symbols.name: SelectDefault
symbols.doc: Select case kinds.

symbols.name: SelectDone
symbols.doc: Select case kinds.

symbols.name: SelectReceive
symbols.doc: Select case kinds.

symbols.name: SelectSend
symbols.doc: Select case kinds.

symbols.name: SelectTimer
symbols.doc: Select case kinds.

symbols.name: ServesHTTP
symbols.doc: What a port serves.

symbols.name: ServesHealth
symbols.doc: What a port serves.

symbols.name: ServesStudio
symbols.doc: What a port serves.

symbols.name: ServiceOf
symbols.doc: ServiceOf returns the service part of a node ID.

symbols.name: Setting
symbols.doc:
Setting is one configuration value kit read when the product started:
kit's own, or one a service of the product declares.

symbols.name: SettingDefault
symbols.doc: Where a setting's value comes from.

symbols.name: SettingEnv
symbols.doc: Where a setting's value comes from.

symbols.name: SettingFile
symbols.doc: Where a setting's value comes from.

symbols.name: SettingKitDev
symbols.doc: Where a setting's value comes from.

symbols.name: SettingOption
symbols.doc: Where a setting's value comes from.

symbols.name: SettingStore
symbols.doc: Where a setting's value comes from.

symbols.name: Snippet
symbols.doc:
Snippet is source code served to a reader of the graph.
Focus and FocusEnd mark the lines a reader asked for, inside the lines
served.

symbols.name: Source
symbols.doc:
Source locates code.
File is relative to its module's root; Line and EndLine bound the
declaration.

symbols.name: Span
symbols.doc:
Span is a finished unit of work, attributed to a node. Only allow-listed,
wire-safe fields travel: no URL, no query string, no private error text.

symbols.name: SplitDoc
StateInfo
symbols.doc:
StateInfo is one state of a workflow.
Terminal marks a state an instance stays in; Count is how many instances
are in it.

symbols.name: Stats
symbols.doc:
Stats are observed counters for a node or an edge.
They are counters: they never move a graph's revision.

symbols.name: StatusError
symbols.doc: Span statuses.

symbols.name: StatusOK
symbols.doc: Span statuses.

symbols.name: Step
symbols.doc:
Step is one transition in an instance's history.
It carries the event, the states it went from and to, and when it fired.

symbols.name: StoreData
symbols.doc:
StoreData is one store's records about a person.
It is one part of what kit.Export gives a person about themselves.

symbols.name: StoreErasure
symbols.doc:
StoreErasure is one store's part of an erasure: the keys of the records
erased, deleted, and held — left in place, as a legal hold asks. A key
may be personal data, which the Studio and the logs never show.

symbols.name: StoreHistory
symbols.doc:
StoreHistory is what a store remembers of its records.
Fields names the fields it keeps former values of; Kept and Bytes weigh
them.

symbols.name: StoreInfo
symbols.doc:
StoreInfo describes a store.
It carries the entity's schema, its backend, its indexes, its privacy and
its history.

symbols.name: StorePrivacy
symbols.doc:
StorePrivacy is what a store keeps of people: whom each record is about,
why, for how long, and — on a runtime graph — what is held and due.

symbols.name: SubscriptionInfo
symbols.doc:
SubscriptionInfo describes a subscription — or a watch (ADR 0008), a
subscription whose deliveries come from stores instead of a topic.

symbols.name: System
symbols.doc:
System is a software system outside the product.
Nodes are the product's nodes that talk to it; Technology says what it runs
on.

symbols.name: TableName
symbols.spelled: func(service string, node string, suffix string) string
symbols.canonical: func(service string, node string, suffix string) string
symbols.doc:
TableName is the table a database keeps a kit table in (ADR 0004): the
service's name — qualified, for a module's —, two underscores and the
node's name, then suffix, '-' and '.' written '_', lower case —
"moderation.intake"'s store "cases" is moderation_intake__cases. A name
the rule cannot keep as it is — upper case, longer than MaxTableLen,
three underscores in a row, SQLite's own prefix — is cut and ends with a
digest of the whole, so it stays one table's. The runtime and the
analyzer name tables with it.

symbols.name: TopicInfo
symbols.doc:
TopicInfo describes a topic.
It carries the message's schema; its subscriptions are the nodes it
delivers to.

symbols.name: Trace
symbols.doc:
Trace is the spans sharing one trace ID, root first.
The root span is the one with no parent in the trace; the others follow it.

symbols.name: TransitionEvent
symbols.doc:
TransitionEvent is one workflow instance moving between states.
It names the workflow, the entity, the event and the states it went from
and to.

symbols.name: TransitionInfo
symbols.doc:
TransitionInfo is one arrow of a workflow.
It names the event that fires it and the states it goes from and to.

symbols.name: TransportCapture
symbols.doc:
TransportCapture keeps every message for the Studio's mailbox and
delivers nothing: the transport of dev and tests.

symbols.name: TransportSMTP
symbols.doc: TransportSMTP delivers to an SMTP relay.

symbols.name: TriggerCreate
symbols.doc: TriggerCreate is the entry of a new instance into the initial state.

symbols.name: TriggerEvent
symbols.doc: TriggerEvent is a transition fired by code, naming an event.

symbols.name: TriggerGuard
symbols.doc:
TriggerGuard is a transition fired when a condition on the entity
holds, checked each time the entity is written.

symbols.name: TriggerTimer
symbols.doc:
TriggerTimer is a transition fired after a duration in a state, or at
an instant the entity carries.

symbols.name: UnderPrefix
symbols.doc:
UnderPrefix is a route declared at path, served under a module's mount
prefix: "/reports" under "/moderation/" is "/moderation/reports", and
under "/" it stays "/reports".

symbols.name: ValidContract
symbols.doc: ValidContract reports whether s names a versioned contract: "render/v1".

symbols.name: ValidName
symbols.doc:
ValidName reports whether s is a legal node name. An endpoint named by its
route is legal as an ID but is not a name a declaration may give.

symbols.name: ValidSegment
symbols.doc:
ValidSegment reports whether s is a legal service, module, binary, role or
library name.

symbols.doc:
The settings kit reads, by the environment variable that sets each: kit's
configuration reads them, the connectors and the architecture name them.

symbols.name: VarAllowedHosts
symbols.doc:
The settings kit reads, by the environment variable that sets each: kit's

symbols.name: VarAnalyze
symbols.doc:
The settings kit reads, by the environment variable that sets each: kit's

symbols.name: VarDataDir
symbols.doc:
The settings kit reads, by the environment variable that sets each: kit's
configuration reads them, the connectors and the architecture name them.

symbols.name: VarDevForced
symbols.doc:
VarDevForced is how kit dev tells the product which of the variables
above it set itself for this launch: their origin is kit dev.

symbols.name: VarEnv
symbols.doc:
The settings kit reads, by the environment variable that sets each: kit's
configuration reads them, the connectors and the architecture name them.

symbols.name: VarLogLevel
symbols.doc:
The settings kit reads, by the environment variable that sets each: kit's
configuration reads them, the connectors and the architecture name them.

symbols.name: VarRetention
symbols.doc:
VarRetention sets what the stores' retention loops do: on, dry-run
or off (ADR 0006).

symbols.name: VarSMTPURL
symbols.doc:
The settings kit reads, by the environment variable that sets each: kit's
configuration reads them, the connectors and the architecture name them.

symbols.name: VarStudio
symbols.doc:
The settings kit reads, by the environment variable that sets each: kit's
configuration reads them, the connectors and the architecture name them.

symbols.name: VarStudioRemote
symbols.doc:
The settings kit reads, by the environment variable that sets each: kit's
configuration reads them, the connectors and the architecture name them.

symbols.name: VarTrustProxy
symbols.doc:
The settings kit reads, by the environment variable that sets each: kit's

symbols.name: Version
symbols.doc:
Version is the schema version of every document in this package.

Version 2 adds the auth, mailer and loop kinds, the sends and wakes edges,
the code level of every node ([CodeInfo]), the C4 context and containers
([Architecture]) and the daemon's own machinery ([Runtime]).

Version 3 adds the secret kind ([SecretInfo]), the uses edge, the secret
span operation, the rotation loop and the store origin of a setting.

Version 4 is the one bump the decisions of issue #17 share. It adds the
port kind ([PortInfo]) and its binding, a declared edge from the port to
what it calls; the endpoint that implements a port
([EndpointInfo].Implements), which has no method and no path; and the
replace mock mode ([MockReplace]). ADR 0004 adds the databases: the store's
database ([StoreInfo].Database), the database container, the database
connector and its adapters, [Runtime].Databases and [Setting].Database.
ADR 0008 adds the modules the app mounts ([Graph].Modules), the module of a
node ([Node].Module) and the Go module of a position outside the product's
([Source].GoModule); and the watch, a subscription fed by stores: its mark
and the stores that feed it ([SubscriptionInfo].Mark,
[SubscriptionInfo].Stores), each drawing a declared delivers edge to it.
ADR 0005 adds the command and query kinds ([CommandInfo], [QueryInfo]),
the dispatches and asks edges, the endpoint that exposes one
([EndpointInfo].Exposes), the read model ([StoreInfo].ReadModel), the
dispatch, ask and handle span operations and the dispatch and ask
controls.

Version 5 is the first the SDK's framework publishes (ADR 0147). It
adds what a product is made of beyond its services: the binary
([KindBinary]) and its process roles ([KindRole]), the short CLI command
([KindCLI]), the listener that is not HTTP ([KindListener]), the library
shared between components ([KindLibrary]) and the presentation
([KindPresentation]); the edge between two roles of a product, which
carries a versioned contract ([EdgeContracts], [Edge].Contract); and the
grammar every ID follows, written once ([ID], [ParseID]). It removes what
the Studio no longer does (D13): the respond, fail and delay mock modes,
the control event and its payload — a [Mock] is a test's replacement only.

symbols.name: ViaBind

symbols.name: ViaFallback

symbols.doc: Wake source kinds of a declared loop, and why a loop of kit's ran.

symbols.doc:
WorkflowInfo describes a state machine bound to a store.
It carries the states and the transitions between them, and the store it
lives in.

symbols.name: AccessAnyUser
symbols.doc:
AccessAnyUser is kit.AnyUser(): any signed-in user may run it — the
operation asks for one.

symbols.name: AccessAnyone
symbols.doc:
AccessAnyone is kit.Anyone(): whoever reaches the route may run the

"github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/connectors/postgres".

fields.doc: Driver is the Go driver it links: "github.com/jackc/pgx/v5".

AdapterMessage is a module a connector plugs a product in through: an engine,

the product that imports its driver.

symbols.spelled: struct{Status string "json:\"status\""; Error string "json:\"error,omitempty\""; At *time.Time "json:\"at,omitempty\""; Packages int "json:\"packages,omitempty\""; TookMs float64 "json:\"tookMs,omitempty\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{Status string "json:\"status\""; Error string "json:\"error,omitempty\""; At *time.Time "json:\"at,omitempty\""; Packages int "json:\"packages,omitempty\""; TookMs float64 "json:\"tookMs,omitempty\""}

fields.doc: Status is "pending", "running", "ok", "failed" or "unavailable".

fields.doc: Error explains a failed or unavailable analysis.

AnalysisResult reports the status of static analysis.
It says whether the analyzer ran, how long it took, and the error that
stopped it.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the product name given to kit.NewApp.

fields.name: Module
fields.doc: Module is the Go module path of the product.

fields.name: Root
fields.doc:
Root is the absolute module root on the machine that produced the
graph. Present in dev only: it is what an editor link needs, and what a
production graph must not leak.

fields.name: Env
fields.doc: Env is "dev" or "production".

fields.name: Kit
fields.doc: Kit is the kit version that produced the graph.

fields.name: Go
fields.doc: Go is the Go version the product was built with.

fields.name: StartedAt
fields.doc: StartedAt is when the process started, for a runtime graph.

fields.name: Build
fields.doc:
Build says what the binary was built from: the product, kit and the
SDK kit depends on.

symbols.doc:
AppMessage identifies the product and the machine that described it.
It names the module, the environment and the build the graph was taken
from.

symbols.name: ArchitectureMessage

fields.name: People
fields.doc: People are the humans the product serves.

fields.name: Systems
fields.doc:
Systems are the software systems outside the product it talks to, or
that talk to it.

fields.name: Containers
fields.doc: Containers are the product's runnable and storage units.

fields.name: Links
fields.doc: Links are the relationships between people, systems and containers.

symbols.doc:
ArchitectureMessage is the product at the two outer levels of the C4 model.

Context (level 1) is the product as one box, the people who use it and the
systems it depends on. Containers (level 2) is what the product is
deployed as: the process, the frontend its browser runs, the volume its
data lives on. Components (level 3) are the nodes, grouped by service; code
(level 4) is each node's [CodeResult].

kit derives all of it from the declarations — a frontend implies a person
with a browser, a mailer an SMTP relay, a data directory a volume, a
database its own container — so it is exactly as true as the rest of the
graph.

symbols.name: AuthOptional
symbols.doc:
AuthOptional endpoints run the auth handler when credentials are
present, and serve anonymous callers too.

symbols.name: AuthRequired
symbols.doc:
AuthRequired endpoints run only for an authenticated caller; the others
are answered 401 before the handler runs.

symbols.name: AuthSpec

fields.name: Credentials
fields.doc:
Credentials is the type the handler reads: its fields are tagged
cookie:"…" or header:"…".

fields.name: Data
fields.doc:
Data is the type of what the handler says about the caller, which
endpoints read with kit.AuthData.

fields.name: Endpoints
fields.doc: Endpoints counts the endpoints that ask for authentication.

symbols.doc:
AuthSpec describes the app's authentication handler.
Credentials says what it reads from a request; Endpoints are the ones
behind it.

symbols.name: BinaryID
symbols.doc: BinaryID is the ID of a binary.

symbols.name: BinaryScope
symbols.doc: BinaryScope prefixes the ID of a binary and of its roles.

symbols.name: BinarySpec

fields.name: Package
fields.doc: Package is the Go package of its main.

fields.name: Roles
fields.doc:
Roles are the IDs of its process roles, in declaration order; the
first is the one it runs with no role argument.

symbols.doc:

symbols.doc:
ConnectorMessage is something a product plugs into, as the product declares it:
how it is reached, what it reaches out to, where it keeps its data. The
Studio shows a connector's pages and widgets only when the product has
one: a command-line tool has no requests to list, a service without a
mailer no mailbox.

A connector says what the code declares, never what an environment
supplies. The relay a mailer delivers through, the directory a store
writes to, the address kit listens on are facts of the running
environment — [MailerSpec], [StoreSpec], the [ArchitectureMessage] and [RuntimeMessage]
carry those. So a connector is a pure function of the nodes
([ConnectorsOf]), and never moves a graph's revision.

TLS is the TLS mode its URL writes: "verify-full"; "none" when it is
written off; empty when the URL leaves it to the driver, or when the
database is a file.

fields.name: Pool
fields.doc:
Pool is database/sql's own count of its connections, sampled when the
graph was built.

fields.name: Migrations
fields.doc:
Migrations are its sets of migrations, kit's first, as the start —
or the last sample — found them.

symbols.doc:
DatabaseMessage is one database the app declares (kit.Database), as the running
process found it. Its URL is never shown: where it was found, the engine,
the address and the TLS mode are.

symbols.name: DatabaseOpen
symbols.doc:
DatabaseOpen: the pool is open, its migrations ran, it answered its
check at start.

symbols.name: DatabaseUnset
symbols.doc:
DatabaseUnset: no URL, in dev. Its stores stay in the data directory
and nothing is opened.

symbols.name: DevBuildMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{BuiltAt *time.Time "json:\"builtAt,omitempty\""; BuildMs float64 "json:\"buildMs,omitempty\""; Rebuilds int "json:\"rebuilds,omitempty\""; Changed []string "json:\"changed,omitempty\""; More int "json:\"more,omitempty\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{BuiltAt *time.Time "json:\"builtAt,omitempty\""; BuildMs float64 "json:\"buildMs,omitempty\""; Rebuilds int "json:\"rebuilds,omitempty\""; Changed []string "json:\"changed,omitempty\""; More int "json:\"more,omitempty\""}

fields.name: BuiltAt
fields.doc: BuiltAt is when the build finished.

fields.name: BuildMs
fields.doc: BuildMs is how long it took.

fields.name: Rebuilds
fields.doc:
Rebuilds counts the builds of this kit dev session, this one
included: 1 is the first start.

fields.name: Changed
fields.doc:
Changed are the files whose change triggered this build, relative to
the module root, at most 20.

fields.name: More
fields.doc: More counts the changed files beyond Changed.

symbols.doc:
DevBuildMessage is one build of `kit dev`: when, how long, and why.
It lets the Studio say what changed and how long the reload took.

symbols.name: DiagnosticMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{Severity string "json:\"severity\""; Message string "json:\"message\""; Texts map[string]string "json:\"texts,omitempty\""; Node string "json:\"node,omitempty\""; Source *SourceMessage "json:\"source,omitempty\""}

fields.name: Severity
fields.doc: Severity is "error" or "warning". An error refuses to start the app.

fields.name: Message
fields.doc: Message says what is wrong and how to fix it, in English.

fields.name: Texts
fields.doc:
Texts is the message in each language kit speaks, by language: "en",
"fr". The Studio shows its reader's.

fields.name: Node
fields.doc: Node is the node concerned, when there is one.

fields.name: Source
fields.doc: Source is where the problem is.

symbols.doc:
DiagnosticMessage is a problem found while building the graph.
It names the node or the file it is about, and how serious it is.

symbols.name: EdgeAsks
symbols.doc:
EdgeAsks targets a query: the source asks it. From an endpoint that
exposes the query, or from a port bound to it, it is declared.

symbols.name: EdgeCalls
symbols.doc:
EdgeCalls targets an endpoint or a port. From a port, it is the port's
binding — what the port calls — and it is declared.

symbols.name: EdgeContracts
symbols.doc:
EdgeContracts goes from one process role to another it talks to —
through a socket, a pipe, a command line —, and names the versioned
contract they share in [EdgeMessage.Contract]. It is the only edge between two
roles (D22). Declared.

symbols.name: EdgeDelivers
symbols.doc:
EdgeDelivers goes from a topic to each of its subscriptions, and from a
store to each watch it feeds (ADR 0008). Declared.

symbols.name: EdgeDispatches
symbols.doc:
EdgeDispatches targets a command: the source dispatches it. From an
endpoint that exposes the command, or from a port bound to it, it is
declared.

symbols.name: EdgeID
symbols.spelled: func(from string, kind EdgeKind, to string, label string) string
symbols.canonical: func(from string, kind github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/model/internal/core.EdgeKind, to string, label string) string
symbols.doc:
EdgeID builds the ID of an edge. The label is part of the identity: two
transitions of one workflow fired from one endpoint are two edges.

symbols.name: EdgeImports
symbols.doc:
EdgeImports goes from a component to a library it may import (D19).
Declared.

symbols.name: EdgeKind
symbols.doc:
EdgeKind says how two nodes relate.
It is a wire format — the graph's JSON and the Studio's TypeScript unions
carry these names —, so it stays a string.

symbols.name: EdgeMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{ID string "json:\"id\""; From string "json:\"from\""; To string "json:\"to\""; Kind EdgeKind "json:\"kind\""; Label string "json:\"label,omitempty\""; Contract string "json:\"contract,omitempty\""; Declared bool "json:\"declared,omitempty\""; Static []SourceMessage "json:\"static,omitempty\""; Observed *StatsMessage "json:\"observed,omitempty\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{ID string "json:\"id\""; From string "json:\"from\""; To string "json:\"to\""; Kind github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/model/internal/core.EdgeKind "json:\"kind\""; Label string "json:\"label,omitempty\""; Contract string "json:\"contract,omitempty\""; Declared bool "json:\"declared,omitempty\""; Static []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/model/internal/core.SourceMessage "json:\"static,omitempty\""; Observed *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/model/internal/core.StatsMessage "json:\"observed,omitempty\""}

fields.name: ID
fields.doc: ID is "<from>|<kind>|<to>" or "<from>|<kind>|<to>|<label>".

fields.name: From
fields.doc: From is the source node ID.

fields.name: To
fields.doc: To is the target node ID.

fields.name: Kind
fields.doc: Kind says how the two relate.

fields.name: Label
fields.doc:
Label refines the kind: the event of a transition ("create" for a new
instance), or "direct" for a call that bypasses an endpoint.

fields.name: Contract
fields.doc:
Contract names the versioned contract of an [EdgeContracts] edge:
"<name>/v<major>", "render/v1".

fields.name: Declared
fields.doc: Declared is set when the edge exists by construction.

fields.name: Static
fields.doc: Static lists the call sites the analyzer found, sorted.

fields.name: Observed
fields.doc: Observed is present once the edge was seen at runtime.

symbols.doc:
EdgeMessage is one relation, with the evidence for it.
Declared, Static and Observed say whether construction, the code or the
runtime knows it.

symbols.name: EdgePersists
symbols.doc: EdgePersists goes from a workflow to the store it lives in. Declared.

symbols.name: EdgePublishes
symbols.doc: EdgePublishes targets a topic.

symbols.name: EdgeReads
symbols.doc: EdgeReads targets a store the source reads from.

symbols.name: EdgeRenders
symbols.doc: EdgeRenders goes from a presentation to what it renders. Declared.

symbols.name: EdgeRuns
symbols.doc:
EdgeRuns goes from a role to what it runs: a CLI command, a listener,
an endpoint's server, a loop. Declared.

symbols.name: EdgeSends
symbols.doc: EdgeSends targets a mailer: the source puts a message in its outbox.

symbols.name: EdgeTransitions
symbols.doc: EdgeTransitions targets a workflow; Label carries the event.

symbols.name: EdgeUses
symbols.doc: EdgeUses targets a secret whose value or keys the source uses.

symbols.name: EdgeWakes
symbols.doc: EdgeWakes goes from a topic to a declared loop it wakes. Declared.

symbols.name: EdgeWrites
symbols.doc: EdgeWrites targets a store the source writes to.

symbols.name: EditMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{Op string "json:\"op\""; Path string "json:\"path\""; From json.RawMessage "json:\"from,omitempty\" kit:\"personal\""; To json.RawMessage "json:\"to,omitempty\" kit:\"personal\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{Op string "json:\"op\""; Path string "json:\"path\""; From encoding/json.RawMessage "json:\"from,omitempty\" kit:\"personal\""; To encoding/json.RawMessage "json:\"to,omitempty\" kit:\"personal\""}
symbols.doc:
EditMessage is one change between two versions of a record, in RFC 6902's
words: Op is add, remove or replace, Path the RFC 6901 JSON pointer of the
member it changes, From its value before and To its value after, as JSON.
A member whose value is not given — a secret's, or in the Studio a
personal or special one — says it changed, never what: From and To are
absent.

fields.name: Method
fields.doc: Method is the HTTP method, upper case; empty for an implementation.

fields.name: Path
fields.doc:
Path is the route pattern, with {wildcards}; empty for an
implementation.

fields.name: Expose
fields.doc: Expose is [ExposePublic] or [ExposePrivate].

fields.name: Auth
fields.doc:
Auth is [AuthRequired], [AuthOptional], or empty when the endpoint
ignores authentication.

fields.name: Request
fields.doc: Request is the input type.

fields.name: Response
fields.doc: Response is the output type.

fields.name: Pipeline
fields.doc:
Pipeline lists the mechanics a request goes through before the
handler, in order.

fields.name: Implements
fields.doc:
Implements is the node ID of the port this endpoint implements
(Service.Implement): an endpoint with no route, reached through the
port.

fields.name: Exposes
fields.doc:
Exposes is the node ID of the command this endpoint dispatches, or of
the query it asks (Command.Expose, Query.Expose): its authentication
is the operation's, and the rest of its pipeline — validation, key,
authorization — the operation's own.

fields.name: Access
fields.doc:
Access is how an exposure says its operation is open on purpose —
[AccessAnyone] or [AccessAnyUser] —; empty when the operation says who
may run it (a permission, a rule), and on any other endpoint.

symbols.doc:
EndpointSpec describes an HTTP endpoint, or the implementation of a port.
It carries the method and path, the request and response schemas, and its
auth.

symbols.name: EngineMySQL
symbols.doc:
The engines a database runs on (ADR 0004): one module each in kit's
repository, the only code that imports its driver.

symbols.name: EnginePostgres
symbols.doc:
The engines a database runs on (ADR 0004): one module each in kit's
repository, the only code that imports its driver.

symbols.name: EngineSQLite
symbols.doc:
The engines a database runs on (ADR 0004): one module each in kit's
repository, the only code that imports its driver.

symbols.name: ErasureMessage

fields.name: Stores
fields.doc: Stores are the stores that kept records about the person.

symbols.doc:
ErasureMessage is what kit.Erase did, store by store.
Stores lists, store by store, what the erasure did there.

fields.name: Seq
fields.doc: Seq increases strictly on one stream; a reader drops what it has seen.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: Type selects the payload.

fields.name: Time
fields.doc: Time is when it happened.

fields.name: Revision
fields.doc: Revision is the graph revision, on hello and graph events.

fields.name: StartedAt
fields.doc:
StartedAt is when the process's current run started, on hello: a new
value means the process restarted, and what the reader knew of the
previous run is stale.

fields.name: Phase
fields.doc: Phase is the process phase, on hello and lifecycle events.

symbols.doc:
Event is one live event. Exactly one of the payload fields matching Type is
set.

symbols.name: EventCensus
symbols.doc: EventCensus reports a workflow's population per state.

symbols.name: EventGraph
symbols.doc: EventGraph reports that the graph structure changed.

symbols.name: EventHello
symbols.doc: EventHello opens every stream and carries the graph revision.

symbols.name: EventLifecycle
symbols.doc:
EventLifecycle reports a lifecycle component moving, or the process
changing phase.

symbols.name: EventLog
symbols.doc: EventLog reports a log record written by product code, in dev.

symbols.name: EventLoop
symbols.doc: EventLoop reports a loop run.

symbols.name: EventMail
symbols.doc: EventMail reports a mail entering the outbox or changing status.

symbols.name: EventSpan
symbols.doc: EventSpan reports one unit of work that finished on a node.

symbols.name: EventTransition
symbols.doc: EventTransition reports a workflow instance changing state.

symbols.name: EventType
symbols.doc:
EventType names the kind of a live event.
It is a wire format — the graph's JSON and the Studio's TypeScript unions
carry these names —, so it stays a string.

symbols.name: ExportedVersionsMessage

fields.name: Record
fields.doc: Record is the record's position in its StoreData's Records.

fields.name: Versions
fields.doc:
Versions are its versions, newest first — the record as it is now
first —, each without its secret members.

symbols.doc:
ExportedVersionsMessage are the versions of one exported record, as a
StoreDataMessage carries them beside its records.

symbols.name: ExposePrivate
symbols.doc:
ExposePrivate endpoints have no route: the implementation of a port
(Service.Implement), reached in process through its port. A graph kit
made before its operations were internal by default also marks so an
endpoint it kept off the listener.

symbols.name: ExposePublic
symbols.doc: ExposePublic endpoints are routed on the product's HTTP listener.

symbols.name: ExternalID
symbols.doc: ExternalID is the id of the node standing for the outside world.

symbols.name: FieldMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{Name string "json:\"name\""; In string "json:\"in,omitempty\""; Type *SchemaMessage "json:\"type\""; Optional bool "json:\"optional,omitempty\""; Rules string "json:\"rules,omitempty\""; Doc string "json:\"doc,omitempty\""; Class string "json:\"class,omitempty\""; Subject bool "json:\"subject,omitempty\""; Moderated bool "json:\"moderated,omitempty\""; Sealed bool "json:\"sealed,omitempty\""; Erased bool "json:\"erased,omitempty\""; History int "json:\"history,omitempty\""}

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the wire name.

fields.name: In
fields.doc:
In is where a request field is read from: "body", "path", "query",
"header" or "cookie". Empty outside requests.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: Type is the member's schema.

fields.name: Optional
fields.doc: Optional is set when the member may be absent.

fields.name: Rules
fields.doc: Rules are the validation rules, as written in the validate tag.

fields.name: Doc
fields.doc: Doc is the field's comment, when the analyzer found one.

fields.name: Class
fields.doc:
Class is what the field holds, as its kit tag says (ADR 0006): one of
the Class constants, or empty when the field is unclassified. A
subject field is personal unless it is special.

fields.name: Subject
fields.doc: Subject marks the field that says whom a record is about.

fields.name: Moderated
fields.doc: Moderated marks content others see and a moderator may act on.

fields.name: Sealed
fields.doc:
Sealed is set when kit keeps the field sealed at rest (ADR 0006 §4):
a personal, special or secret field, or the subject, not plain, of
what kit keeps on disk — a store's entity, a topic's message, a queued
command's input. A store in memory seals nothing.

fields.name: Erased
fields.doc: Erased marks the time kit stamps when it erases the record.

fields.name: History
fields.doc: History is how many former values kit keeps of the field (ADR 0007).

symbols.doc:
FieldMessage is one member of an object schema.
It carries the JSON name, the schema of its value and the classes of its
data.

symbols.name: FileMessage

fields.name: GoModule
fields.doc: GoModule is empty for a file of the product's own module.

symbols.doc:
FileMessage is one file a graph points at: its path, relative to its root — the
product's module, or the Go module [SourceMessage.GoModule] names.

symbols.name: FlameNodeMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{Name string "json:\"name\""; Value float64 "json:\"value\""; Node string "json:\"node,omitempty\""; Children []*FlameNodeMessage "json:\"children,omitempty\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{Name string "json:\"name\""; Value float64 "json:\"value\""; Node string "json:\"node,omitempty\""; Children []*github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/model/internal/core.FlameNodeMessage "json:\"children,omitempty\""}

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the function.

fields.name: Value
fields.doc: Value is its cumulative cost.

fields.name: Node
fields.doc: Node is the node the frame belongs to, when it is a node's code.

fields.name: Children
fields.doc: Children are its callees, highest first.

symbols.doc:
FlameNodeMessage is one frame of a flame graph.
Its children are the frames it called; its value is the samples under it.

symbols.name: FormerMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{Value json.RawMessage "json:\"value,omitempty\" kit:\"personal\""; Until time.Time "json:\"until\""; By string "json:\"by,omitempty\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{Value encoding/json.RawMessage "json:\"value,omitempty\" kit:\"personal\""; Until time.Time "json:\"until\""; By string "json:\"by,omitempty\""}

fields.name: Value
fields.doc:
Value is the field's value then, as JSON; absent for a secret field,
whose former values are never given.

fields.name: Until
fields.doc: Until is when it was replaced, on the app's clock.

fields.name: By
fields.doc:
By is the user who replaced it — kit.UserID —, empty for a write
with no user: a job's, a loop's, kit's own.

symbols.doc:
FormerMessage is one former value of a field that keeps its history: what it
was, until when, and who replaced it.

symbols.name: FrontendSpec

fields.name: Prefix
fields.doc: Prefix is the URL path the assets are served under.

fields.name: Files
fields.doc: Files is how many files are served.

symbols.doc:
FrontendSpec describes static assets served by the product.
It carries the path the assets are served under and where they are read
from.

symbols.name: FuncCostMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{Func string "json:\"func\""; Source *SourceMessage "json:\"source,omitempty\""; Flat float64 "json:\"flat\""; Cum float64 "json:\"cum\""; Node string "json:\"node,omitempty\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{Func string "json:\"func\""; Source *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/model/internal/core.SourceMessage "json:\"source,omitempty\""; Flat float64 "json:\"flat\""; Cum float64 "json:\"cum\""; Node string "json:\"node,omitempty\""}

fields.name: Func
fields.doc: Func is the qualified function name.

fields.name: Source
fields.doc: Source locates it, when it is in the product's module.

fields.name: Flat
fields.doc: Flat is the cost of the function's own code; Cum includes its callees.

fields.name: Node
fields.doc: Node is the node it was attributed to, when one.

symbols.doc:
FuncCostMessage is what one function cost.
It carries the flat and cumulative samples of the function and where it
lives.

symbols.name: GapPurpose
symbols.doc: The gaps a register lists for a store that keeps personal data.

symbols.name: GapRetention
symbols.doc: The gaps a register lists for a store that keeps personal data.

symbols.name: GapSubject
symbols.doc: The gaps a register lists for a store that keeps personal data.

symbols.name: GoroutineGroup
symbols.spelled: struct{Node string "json:\"node,omitempty\""; Loop string "json:\"loop,omitempty\""; State string "json:\"state\""; Count int "json:\"count\""; Top string "json:\"top\""; Stack []string "json:\"stack,omitempty\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{Node string "json:\"node,omitempty\""; Loop string "json:\"loop,omitempty\""; State string "json:\"state\""; Count int "json:\"count\""; Top string "json:\"top\""; Stack []string "json:\"stack,omitempty\""}

fields.name: Node
fields.doc: Node is the node they run for, from their pprof label, when any.

fields.name: Loop
fields.doc: Loop is the loop they are, when kit knows: "http accept", a consumer.

fields.name: State
fields.doc:
State is the runtime's word for what they wait on: "running",
"select", "chan receive", "IO wait", "sleep", "semacquire"…

fields.name: Count
fields.doc: Count is how many goroutines are in the group.

fields.name: Top
fields.doc: Top is the innermost frame that is not the runtime's.

fields.name: Stack
fields.doc: Stack is the group's stack, innermost first, capped.

symbols.doc:
GoroutineGroup is goroutines doing the same thing.
They share one stack; Count says how many run it.

symbols.name: GoroutinesResult

fields.name: At
fields.doc: At is when they were counted.

fields.name: Total
fields.doc: Total is how many goroutines exist.

fields.name: Groups
fields.doc:
Groups are goroutines sharing a node or loop, a state and a top frame,
largest first.

symbols.doc:
GoroutinesResult is every goroutine of the process, grouped by what it runs.
Each group names the node its stack runs in, when one does.

fields.name: Version
fields.doc: Version is always [Version] for a document this package produced.

fields.name: Revision
fields.doc:
Revision changes whenever the structure changes (nodes, edges, sources),
never when only observed statistics move. A reader caches layout on it.

fields.name: App
fields.doc: App identifies the product.

fields.name: Nodes
fields.doc: Nodes are sorted by ID.

fields.name: Edges
fields.doc: Edges are sorted by ID.

fields.name: Catalog
fields.doc: Catalog lists the generic mechanics this kit version offers.

fields.name: Diagnostics
fields.doc: Diagnostics are problems found while building the graph.

fields.name: Runtime
fields.doc: Runtime is present when a running process describes itself.

fields.name: Analysis
fields.doc: Analysis reports the static analysis that enriched this graph.

fields.name: Architecture
fields.doc:
Architecture is the product at C4's two outer levels: who uses it and
what it depends on, and what it is deployed as.

fields.name: Connectors
fields.doc:
Connectors are what the product plugs into, derived from its nodes by
[GraphMessage.Normalize]: the Studio shows their pages and widgets only.

fields.name: ConnectorCatalog
fields.doc:
ConnectorCatalog is every connector this kit version ships, used or
not: what the product may plug into, and what brings each.

fields.name: Modules
fields.doc: Modules are the modules the app mounts (ADR 0008), sorted by name.

symbols.doc:
GraphMessage is the whole product.
It is the JSON document the runtime serves and the analyzer writes; Version
names its shape.

symbols.name: Edge
symbols.doc: Edge returns the edge with the given ID, or nil.

symbols.name: Files
symbols.doc:
Files returns every file the graph points at, each with its root — the
product's module, or another Go module: a module's (ADR 0008), a
library's —, sorted and deduplicated. It is the complete list of files a
reader of this graph may legitimately ask to see, and the source endpoint
serves nothing else.

symbols.name: ModuleOf
symbols.doc: ModuleOf returns the module named name, or nil.

symbols.name: Node
symbols.doc: Node returns the node with the given ID, or nil.

symbols.name: Normalize
symbols.doc:
Normalize sorts nodes, edges and call sites into their canonical order,
fills each workflow transition's callers from the edges, derives the
connectors from the nodes, and recomputes Revision. Two graphs describing the same structure normalize to
the same bytes, whatever order they were built in.

fields.name: Library
fields.doc:
Library is the implementation: "sdk/v1/net/server" — the SDK's engine
accepting and draining the connections, net/http speaking the protocol.

fields.name: Loop
fields.doc:
Loop says how it serves: one accept loop, one goroutine per
connection, written by the library rather than the product.

fields.name: Addr
fields.doc: Addr is the listening address.

fields.name: Middleware
fields.doc:
Middleware is the chain every request goes through before its route,
outermost first.

fields.name: Timeouts
fields.doc:
Timeouts are the server's timeouts, as Go durations: "readHeader",
"read", "write", "idle".

fields.name: Conns
fields.doc:
Conns counts connections: "active" now, "total" ever accepted,
"rejected" by the listener's ceiling. Older graphs carry "new", "idle"
and "hijacked" too.

fields.name: InFlight
fields.doc: InFlight is how many requests are being served.

fields.name: Served
fields.doc: Served counts the requests served since start.

symbols.doc:
HTTPServer is the product's HTTP server, and whose loop serves it.
Its address is the one it listens on; its loop is the node that runs it.

symbols.name: HeldUntilSpec

fields.name: At
fields.doc: At locates the function that gives the instant.

fields.name: Reason
fields.doc:
Reason is the legal ground the declaration gives: "commercial code:
10 years".

symbols.doc:
HeldUntilSpec is the hold a store declares on each of its records, until an
instant the record carries.

fields.name: Store
fields.doc: Store is the store's node ID.

fields.name: Record
fields.doc: Record is the record's reference.

fields.name: Subject
fields.doc:
Subject is the reference of the person the record is about, when it
has one.

fields.name: By
fields.doc: By is who placed it: a user's ID, "cli" or "studio".

fields.name: At
fields.doc: At is when.

symbols.doc:
HoldEvent is one record a legal hold keeps. It carries references only: never
the record's key, its subject's identity, or the hold's reason, which kit
keeps apart.

symbols.name: IDPattern
symbols.doc:
IDPattern is the whole grammar as one regular expression, anchored —
the one the design files' JSON Schema publishes for an ID. Only an
endpoint may be named by its route.

symbols.name: IDValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Module string; Service string; Scope string; Kind NodeKind; Name string}
symbols.canonical: struct{Module string; Service string; Scope string; Kind github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/model/internal/core.NodeKind; Name string}

fields.name: Module
fields.doc:
Module qualifies Service when a module lists it; empty for the
product's own services, and for a module's service named like it.

fields.name: Service
fields.doc:
Service is the service's own name, unqualified; empty for a binary, a
role, a library and [ExternalID].

fields.name: Scope
fields.doc:
Scope is the name of the binary of a binary or a role, or of the
library of a library; empty otherwise.

fields.name: Kind
fields.doc: Kind is the node's kind.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc:
Name is the node's name: the service's for a service, the binary's for
a binary.

symbols.doc:
IDValue is a node's identity, parsed: the one grammar of [IDPattern]. Its
String is the ID it was parsed from.

symbols.name: QualifiedServiceName
symbols.doc:
QualifiedServiceName is the service's ID segment: the qualification
[QualifiedService] applies.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc:
String renders the ID; ParseID(id.String()) is id for every ID ParseID
returned.

symbols.name: IndexSpec

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is how code asks for the index: Store.Lookup(ctx, name, key).

fields.name: Unique
fields.doc:
Unique is set when two entities may not share a key: a write that
would is refused with a conflict.

symbols.doc:
IndexSpec is one secondary index of a store.
Its name is unique in the store; Unique says whether two records may share
a key.

symbols.name: InstanceMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{ID string "json:\"id\""; State string "json:\"state\""; EnteredAt time.Time "json:\"enteredAt\""; History []StepEvent "json:\"history,omitempty\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{ID string "json:\"id\""; State string "json:\"state\""; EnteredAt time.Time "json:\"enteredAt\""; History []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/model/internal/core.StepEvent "json:\"history,omitempty\""}

fields.name: ID
fields.doc: ID is the entity key.

fields.name: State
fields.doc: State is the current state.

fields.name: EnteredAt
fields.doc: EnteredAt is when the instance entered its current state.

fields.name: History
fields.doc: History lists the transitions, oldest first, capped.

symbols.doc:
InstanceMessage is one entity's journey through a workflow.
It carries the entity's key, its current state and the steps that brought
it there.

symbols.name: InvalidID

code.public: The node identifier is not valid

symbols.doc:
InvalidID is returned by [ParseID] for a string the ID grammar does not
match. Its "part" field names what failed — the kind, the service name, the
node name —, never the input.

symbols.name: IsEngine
symbols.doc: IsEngine reports whether backend names an engine a database runs on.

symbols.name: JobSpec

fields.name: Schedule
fields.doc: Schedule is "every 10s" or a five-field cron expression.

fields.name: Kind
fields.doc: Kind is "interval" or "cron".

symbols.doc:
JobSpec describes a scheduled job.
It carries the fixed interval or the cron expression that schedules it.

symbols.name: JournalCheckMessage

fields.name: Entries
fields.doc: Entries is how many entries the journal holds.

fields.name: BrokenAt
fields.doc:
BrokenAt is the sequence number where the chain breaks: an entry
changed, or one removed before it. Zero when the chain holds.

symbols.doc:
JournalCheckMessage is what verifying the journal's chain found.
A broken chain names the first entry whose hash does not follow.

symbols.name: JournalDelete
symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

fields.name: Seq
fields.doc: Seq numbers the entries from 1, with no gap.

fields.name: At
fields.doc: At is when, on the app's clock.

fields.name: Op
fields.doc: Op is one of the Journal constants.

fields.name: DryRun
fields.doc:
DryRun marks what the retention would have done under
KIT_RETENTION=dry-run: nothing changed.

fields.name: Store
fields.doc: Store is the store's node ID.

fields.name: Record
fields.doc: Record is the record's reference; Subject its subject's.

fields.name: By
fields.doc:
By is who: a user's ID, the node that called, "retention", "cli" or
"studio".

fields.name: Hash
fields.doc:
Hash is the entry's link in the chain: SHA-256 of the previous
entry's hash and this entry.

symbols.doc:
JournalEntryEvent is one operation of the privacy journal: what was done,
where, by whom and when, with references only — never an identity, a
value or a key. Each entry is chained to the previous one by SHA-256.

symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.name: JournalRead
symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.name: JournalRelease
symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.name: JournalShred
symbols.doc: The operations of the privacy journal.

symbols.name: KindAuth
symbols.doc:
KindAuth is the app's authentication handler: it turns a request's
credentials into a user, in front of every endpoint that asks for one.

symbols.name: KindBinary
symbols.doc:
KindBinary is one executable the product ships. It holds process
roles; its ID is "binary:<name>".

symbols.name: KindCLI
symbols.doc:
KindCLI is a short command-line command: it parses its arguments,
runs once and exits with a typed status.

symbols.name: KindCommand
symbols.doc:
KindCommand is an operation that changes something: a typed input, a
typed result, one handler, the pipeline of its kind. It is dispatched,
on its caller's goroutine or through its own queue.

symbols.name: KindEndpoint
symbols.doc: KindEndpoint is an HTTP endpoint with typed request and response.

symbols.name: KindExternal
symbols.doc: KindExternal stands for everything outside the product.

symbols.name: KindFrontend
symbols.doc: KindFrontend is static assets served by the product.

symbols.name: KindJob
symbols.doc: KindJob is scheduled work: a fixed interval or a cron expression.

symbols.name: KindLibrary
symbols.doc:
KindLibrary is a package shared between components, declared so the
components that use it are allowed to import it. Its ID is
"library:<name>".

symbols.name: KindListener
symbols.doc:
KindListener accepts connections that are not HTTP: a private Unix
socket, a named pipe. It is an inbound port like an endpoint.

symbols.name: KindLoop
symbols.doc:
KindLoop is a long-running loop of the daemon: declared (kit owns the
wait, the product the work) or hand-written (a goroutine kit supervises).

symbols.name: KindMailer
symbols.doc:
KindMailer is outbound mail: a durable outbox, and the transport that
empties it — SMTP, or the capture of dev and tests.

symbols.name: KindPort
symbols.doc:
KindPort is an operation a service needs and does not implement: a
typed request, a typed response, a name. What it calls — another
service's endpoint, the app's binding, its own fallback — is decided
when the app starts, and drawn as a declared edge from the port.

symbols.name: KindPresentation
symbols.doc:
KindPresentation turns a service's results into what a reader sees:
a rendered line, a page, a report.

symbols.name: KindQuery
symbols.doc:
KindQuery is an operation that reads and changes nothing: a typed
input, a typed result, one handler. It is asked.

symbols.name: KindRole
symbols.doc:
KindRole is one process role of a binary — "statusline" and
"statusline daemon" are two roles of one binary. Its root package is
generated wiring; two roles talk through their contract only. Its ID
is "binary:<binary>/role/<name>".

symbols.name: KindSecret
symbols.doc:
KindSecret is a secret the product declares: provided by the operator,
or generated by kit and rotated on a schedule. Its value is never in a
graph.

symbols.name: KindService
symbols.doc: KindService groups the nodes of one bounded context.

symbols.name: KindStore
symbols.doc: KindStore is a typed, keyed collection of entities.

symbols.name: KindSubscription
symbols.doc: KindSubscription consumes one topic.

symbols.name: KindTopic
symbols.doc: KindTopic is an asynchronous, at-least-once message channel.

symbols.name: KindWorkflow
symbols.doc: KindWorkflow is a state machine over the entities of one store.

symbols.name: LibraryID
symbols.doc: LibraryID is the ID of a library.

symbols.name: LibraryScope
symbols.doc: LibraryScope prefixes the ID of a library.

symbols.name: LibrarySpec

fields.name: Package
fields.doc: Package is its Go import path.

symbols.doc:
LibrarySpec is a package shared between components (D19): the
[NodeEntity.Library] of a [KindLibrary] node.

symbols.name: LinkMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{From string "json:\"from\""; To string "json:\"to\""; Label string "json:\"label\""; Technology string "json:\"technology,omitempty\""; Nodes []string "json:\"nodes,omitempty\""; Connectors []string "json:\"connectors,omitempty\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{From string "json:\"from\""; To string "json:\"to\""; Label string "json:\"label\""; Technology string "json:\"technology,omitempty\""; Nodes []string "json:\"nodes,omitempty\""; Connectors []string "json:\"connectors,omitempty\""}

fields.name: From
fields.doc: From is the ID of a person, system or container.

fields.name: To
fields.doc: To is the ID of a person, system or container.

fields.name: Label
fields.doc: Label says what the relationship is: "Reads and writes".

fields.name: Technology
fields.doc: Technology says how: "JSON over HTTP", "SMTP", "file I/O".

fields.name: Nodes
fields.doc: Nodes are the nodes whose edges make the link true.

fields.name: Connectors
fields.doc:
Connectors are the connectors the link is made of: one link from the
process to the data directory carries the stores, the queues and the
mail outbox.

symbols.doc:
LinkMessage is a relationship between two elements of the architecture. The
process's link to a database, "Reads and writes", carries the database
connector, and the store connector once stores live on it.

fields.name: Network
fields.doc: Network is one of the Network constants.

fields.name: Contract
fields.doc: Contract is the versioned contract spoken on it: "render/v1".

fields.name: Peer
fields.doc:
Peer says who may connect: "owner" (the process's own user), or the
declared list, never "anyone".

fields.name: Role
fields.doc: Role is the ID of the role that runs it.

symbols.doc:
ListenerSpec is a listener that is not HTTP: the [NodeEntity.Listener] of a
[KindListener] node — its network, its contract, who may connect.

fields.name: Seq
fields.doc: Seq orders records; it only increases.

fields.name: Time
fields.doc: Time is when it was written.

fields.name: Level
fields.doc: Level is "debug", "info", "warn" or "error".

fields.name: Message
fields.doc: Message is the record's message.

fields.name: Node
fields.doc: Node is the node whose code wrote it.

fields.name: TraceID
fields.doc: TraceID and SpanID correlate it with a span.

fields.name: Attrs
fields.doc: Attrs are the record's attributes, as text, secrets redacted.

symbols.doc:
LogRecordMessage is one log record written by product code through kit.Log, kept
in dev so the Studio can show a request's logs beside its spans.

symbols.name: LoopDeclared
symbols.doc:
LoopDeclared is Service.Loop: kit owns the wait — the wake sources are
data, so the diagram draws them — and the product owns the work.

symbols.name: LoopGoroutine
symbols.doc:
LoopGoroutine is Service.Go: the product wrote the whole loop; kit
starts it, stops it, restarts it after a failure, and reads its select
statements to draw what it waits on.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name identifies the loop.

fields.name: Node
fields.doc: Node is the node the loop drives.

fields.name: Kind
fields.doc: Kind is one of the Loop constants.

fields.name: Provenance
fields.doc: Provenance is one of the Provenance constants.

fields.name: Library
fields.doc:
Library names the code that loops, for a library or kit loop:
"net/http", "sdk/v1/app/scheduler", "sdk/v1/data/queue",
"sdk/v1/app/mail/spool", "sdk/v1/app/statemachine", "kit".

fields.name: State
fields.doc: State is one of the Loop state constants.

fields.name: LastWake
fields.doc:
LastWake is why the last run started: "interval", "topic",
"deadline", "manual", "start".

fields.name: Restarts
fields.doc: Restarts counts supervised restarts, for a hand-written loop.

fields.name: Schedule
fields.doc: Schedule is human text: "every 10s", "*/5 * * * *", "on publish · poll 5s".

fields.name: Runs
fields.doc: Runs counts completed runs.

fields.name: Errors
fields.doc: Errors counts failed runs.

fields.name: Missed
fields.doc: Missed counts due instants dropped because they had already passed.

fields.name: Skipped
fields.doc: Skipped counts fires skipped because the previous run was still going.

fields.name: LastRun
fields.doc: LastRun is when the last run started.

fields.name: LastMs
fields.doc: LastMs is how long the last run took.

fields.name: NextRun
fields.doc: NextRun is when the next run is due, when it is known.

fields.name: LastError
fields.doc: LastError is the public message of the last failure.

symbols.doc:
LoopMessage is one recurring piece of the daemon's internal loop: a job, a
workflow's timer sweep, a subscription's consumer, the HTTP accept loop, a
declared or hand-written loop.

MechanicMessage is a generic building block, backed by an SDK package, that a node

pipeline lists the ones it uses.

symbols.name: Merge
symbols.doc:
Merge enriches a graph with what another description of the same product
knows. base is authoritative on which nodes exist — a runtime graph describes
what the process actually serves —, on the modules it mounts, on what each
of its ports calls and on which stores feed each of its watches: the app
chose them when it started, where the analysis only reads the same rules
over the whole module. extra, typically
the static analysis, contributes documentation, handler ranges — an
authorization function's too —, transition callers and the edges it
found. Nodes only extra knows about are dropped: code that is compiled but
not mounted in this app is not part of this product — save a node of a
module's service the base mounts, which a package the binary does not link
declares: a warning says so.

symbols.name: Mermaid
symbols.doc:
Mermaid renders the architecture of a graph as a Mermaid flowchart: one
subgraph per service — a module's inside the module's own, ADR 0008 —, one
arrow per edge. GitHub renders it in Markdown, which makes a product's
README carry its own, always regenerable, diagram.

Each kind has its shape: an endpoint a box (marked "auth" when it asks for
a user; an implementation of a port by its name), a store a cylinder, a
topic a flag, a subscription a parallelogram (a watch, ADR 0008, marked
with the mark it watches — its stores' arrows say where from), a
workflow a hexagon, a job a
stadium, the auth handler a trapezoid — a gate —, a mailer a subroutine
box, a declared loop a circle, a hand-written loop a double circle, a
port an inverted trapezoid — a socket, UML's required interface —, a
command a parallelogram leaning back — a subscription's leans forward —,
marked "queued" when it waits in its queue, and a query a rhombus, a
question. An arrow is solid when it exists by construction or was
observed, dotted when only the code says so — or when it is a port's
binding to its own fallback, the default the app may replace, as the
Studio draws it.

symbols.doc:
MockReplace is the one mode a [MockMessage] has: a test's kit.Replace, a typed

ModeSync is handled on its caller's goroutine: Dispatch returns the
handler's result.

implements.

It is the Privacy page's data: the register, the holds and the journal's
state.

fields.name: OS

fields.name: MaxProcs

fields.name: Goroutines

the heap, the stacks, the runtime's own structures.

fields.name: TotalAllocBytes

fields.name: GCCycles
fields.doc: GCCycles counts completed garbage collections.

fields.name: LastGC

fields.name: GCPauseP99Ms

fields.name: UptimeMs

ProcessSpec is the Go process a product runs in.
It carries the runtime's figures — goroutines, heap, GC, CPU — taken at At.

personal data and how they go — the register's time limits, GDPR
art. 30(1)(f); empty when it gave none.

symbols.doc:
ProductRetentionSpec is a retention the product keeps itself, as it says
it.

symbols.name: ProfileCLI
symbols.doc:
ProfileCLI parses its arguments, runs once and exits with a typed
status. It starts no listener and no loop outlives it.

a private socket, a pipe — and runs its loops.

symbols.name: ProfileHeap

fields.name: At

fields.name: DurationMs

fields.name: Unit
fields.doc: Unit is what the values count: "ms" of CPU, "bytes" of heap.

fields.name: Total
fields.doc: Total is the sum of every sample.

fields.name: Nodes
fields.doc: Nodes are the costs attributed to nodes, highest first.

fields.name: Unattributed

garbage collector, kit itself, idle loops.

fields.name: Flame
fields.doc: Flame is the call tree, root first, pruned below 0.5% of Total.

every sample is attributed to the node whose code was running — through
the pprof label kit puts on every handler, subscription, job and loop run,
or, for the heap, which carries no label, through the node's code functions
on the sample's stack.

symbols.name: ProfileServer
symbols.doc:

product, and the only profile that opens a TCP listener.

sweep, a declared loop's wake cycle.

symbols.doc:
ProvenanceLibrary loops are written by a library: net/http's accept
loop, the SDK scheduler, the SDK queue consumer.

symbols.name: ProvenanceProduct
symbols.doc: ProvenanceProduct loops are written by hand in the product: Service.Go.

symbols.name: QualifiedService
symbols.doc:

module's own name for the service named like it, "<module>.<service>"
otherwise. The runtime and the analyzer both qualify with it.

first, by the field's JSON pointer — a secret field's without their
values, a personal or special one's redacted.

field that says whom each record is about.

fields.name: SubjectDoc
fields.doc: SubjectDoc is that field's comment, when the analyzer read it.

itself (kit.RetentionByProduct), in its own words: no retention gap,

fields.name: Security

fields.name: Gaps

nothing: how a new retention is deployed over old data.

symbols.name: RetentionOff

symbols.name: RetentionOn
symbols.doc: RetentionOn erases and deletes what is due: the default.

from: a record's closing, say.

from an instant the record carries (After or Setting, and Since), or at an
instant a function gives (At).

that value came from.

fields.name: Boot
fields.doc:
Boot is what kit did to start the product, step by step, as it ran;
the lifecycle components it then started are Components.

fields.name: Databases
fields.doc:
Databases are the databases the app declares, as this run found them:
each one's state, readiness, pool and migrations.

symbols.doc:
RuntimeMessage is what a running process says about itself: the daemon's own state
and its internal loop.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc:
Type is "object", "array", "map", "string", "integer", "number",
"boolean" or "any".

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the qualified Go type name, for named types.

fields.name: Format
fields.doc: Format refines a scalar: "date-time", "duration", "int64"…

fields.name: Fields
fields.doc: Fields are the members of an object.

fields.name: Items
fields.doc: Items is the element type of an array.

fields.name: Values
fields.doc: Values is the value type of a map.

fields.name: Enum
fields.doc: Enum lists the allowed values, when they are known.

fields.name: Ref
fields.doc: Ref names a type already described higher up, to break a cycle.

fields.name: Nullable
fields.doc:
Nullable says a nil value is written null: a pointer, a slice, a map,
an interface — unless its member leaves it out (omitempty, omitzero).

symbols.doc:
SchemaMessage describes a Go type as it appears on the wire.
It is a JSON-Schema-like shape: a kind, its fields or elements, and its Go
type.

symbols.name: SealedPlaceholder
symbols.doc:
SealedPlaceholder is what the Studio receives in place of a value kit
keeps sealed at rest — a record's member in the data browser, a former
value —: never the value, nor its box (ADR 0006 §9). A value it opens and
may not show is "[redacted]".

symbols.name: SecretFromEnv
symbols.doc:
SecretFromEnv is the environment: the variable, or the file its _FILE
form names.

symbols.name: SecretFromFile
symbols.doc:
SecretFromFile is kit's encrypted file store: KIT_SECRETS=file:<dir>,
or .kit/secrets/dev in dev.

symbols.name: SecretFromMemory
symbols.doc:
SecretFromMemory is a store in the process's memory: a test, or
KIT_SECRETS=memory. A generated secret is made again at every start.

symbols.name: SecretFromStore
symbols.doc: SecretFromStore is a store the product's code gave kit.

symbols.name: SecretGenerated
symbols.doc:
SecretGenerated is made by kit and rotated on a schedule: a signing or
sealing key.

symbols.name: SecretProvided
symbols.doc: SecretProvided is given by the operator: an SMTP URL, an API token.

fields.name: Origin
fields.doc: Origin is [SecretProvided] or [SecretGenerated].

fields.name: Variable
fields.doc:
Variable is the environment variable that provides it, or — for a
generated secret — pins it: TODO_SMTP_URL, or TODO_SMTP_URL_FILE naming
a file.

fields.name: Bytes
fields.doc: Bytes is the size of each version of a generated secret.

fields.name: RotateEvery
fields.doc:
RotateEvery is how often kit makes a new version of a generated
secret, as a Go duration.

fields.name: Keep
fields.doc: Keep is how many versions a rotation leaves, the new one included.

fields.name: Optional
fields.doc:
Optional: a provided secret the product can do without
(kit.Optional) — found nowhere, it is absent, and the start goes on.

fields.name: From
fields.doc:
From is where the running app found it: one of the SecretFrom
constants, on a runtime graph. Empty when it is found nowhere — for an
optional secret, absent.

fields.name: Version
fields.doc: Version is the number of its current version, from 1.

fields.name: Created
fields.doc:
Created is when the current version was made; the environment does
not say when a variable was set.

fields.name: Versions
fields.doc: Versions is how many versions are kept.

fields.name: NextRotation
fields.doc:
NextRotation is when kit rotates it next. Absent when kit does not
rotate it: provided, pinned by the environment, or in a store kit
cannot write.

fields.name: Pinned
fields.doc:
Pinned: a generated secret the environment provides — kit uses it and
does not rotate it.

fields.name: Rotations
fields.doc: Rotations counts the rotations this process made.

fields.name: Problem
fields.doc: Problem says why it cannot be used, on a runtime graph.

symbols.doc:
SecretSpec describes a declared secret: how it is made, where it lives,
its versions — never its value.

symbols.name: SegmentPattern
symbols.doc: SegmentPattern is a service, module, binary, role or library name.

symbols.name: SelectCaseMessage

fields.name: Text
fields.doc: Text is the case as written: "<-ticker.C", "job := <-jobs".

fields.name: Kind
fields.doc: Kind is one of the Select constants.

fields.name: Source
fields.doc: Source is where the case is.

symbols.doc:
SelectCaseMessage is one case of a select statement in a hand-written loop.
The analyzer reads it from the loop's body; Kind says what the case waits
on.

symbols.name: SelectDefault
symbols.doc: Select case kinds.

symbols.name: SelectDone
symbols.doc: Select case kinds.

symbols.name: SelectReceive
symbols.doc: Select case kinds.

symbols.name: SelectSend
symbols.doc: Select case kinds.

symbols.name: SelectTimer
symbols.doc: Select case kinds.

symbols.name: ServesHTTP
symbols.doc: What a port serves.

symbols.name: ServesHealth
symbols.doc: What a port serves.

symbols.name: ServesStudio
symbols.doc: What a port serves.

symbols.name: ServiceOf
symbols.doc: ServiceOf returns the service part of a node ID.

symbols.name: SettingDefault
symbols.doc: Where a setting's value comes from.

symbols.name: SettingEnv
symbols.doc: Where a setting's value comes from.

symbols.name: SettingFile
symbols.doc: Where a setting's value comes from.

symbols.name: SettingKitDev
symbols.doc: Where a setting's value comes from.

symbols.name: SettingMessage

symbols.canonical: struct{Name string "json:\"name\""; Value string "json:\"value,omitempty\""; From string "json:\"from\""; Service string "json:\"service,omitempty\""; Key string "json:\"key,omitempty\""; Type string "json:\"type,omitempty\""; Detail string "json:\"detail,omitempty\""; Secret bool "json:\"secret,omitempty\""; Option string "json:\"option,omitempty\""; Flag string "json:\"flag,omitempty\""; Database string "json:\"database,omitempty\""}

fields.name: Name
fields.doc:
Name is the environment variable that sets it: "KIT_ADDR",
"TODO_BASE_URL".

fields.name: Value
fields.doc: Value is what kit uses. A secret's is left out: Secret says so.

fields.name: From
fields.doc: From is one of the Setting constants.

fields.name: Service
fields.doc: Service declared it; empty for kit's own.

fields.name: Key
fields.doc:
Key is a declared setting's name, its key in a configuration file:
"base-url". A module's is qualified with the module's name,
"moderation.tdb-url": kit.Set's key, and in a file "tdb-url" under
"moderation:" (ADR 0008).

fields.name: Type
fields.doc:
Type is what a declared setting holds: text, bool, int, number,
duration or list.

fields.name: Detail
fields.doc:
Detail is the configuration file that gave the value, when From is
SettingFile: "config/production.yaml".

fields.name: Secret
fields.doc: Secret: the value is withheld.

fields.name: Option
fields.doc:
Option is the AppOption that sets it in code, when there is one:
"kit.Listen". Code wins over the environment.

fields.name: Flag
fields.doc:
Flag is the kit dev flag that sets it in dev, when there is one:
"-addr".

fields.name: Database
fields.doc:
Database is the database the setting configures, when kit declares it
for one (kit.Database): its URL, its pool, its timeouts.

symbols.doc:
SettingMessage is one configuration value kit read when the product started:
kit's own, or one a service of the product declares.

symbols.name: SettingOption
symbols.doc: Where a setting's value comes from.

symbols.name: SettingStore
symbols.doc: Where a setting's value comes from.

symbols.name: SnippetMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{File string "json:\"file\""; StartLine int "json:\"startLine\""; Focus int "json:\"focus\""; FocusEnd int "json:\"focusEnd,omitempty\""; Lines []string "json:\"lines\""; Language string "json:\"language\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{File string "json:\"file\""; StartLine int "json:\"startLine\""; Focus int "json:\"focus\""; FocusEnd int "json:\"focusEnd,omitempty\""; Lines []string "json:\"lines\""; Language string "json:\"language\""}

fields.name: File
fields.doc: File is relative to App.Root.

fields.name: StartLine
fields.doc: StartLine is the 1-based line of Lines[0].

fields.name: Focus
fields.doc: Focus is the first line of the range asked for.

fields.name: FocusEnd
fields.doc: FocusEnd is the last line of the range asked for.

fields.name: Lines
fields.doc: Lines are the file's lines around the focus, without terminators.

fields.name: Language
fields.doc: Language is the highlighter language: "go", "javascript"…

symbols.doc:
SnippetMessage is source code served to a reader of the graph.
Focus and FocusEnd mark the lines a reader asked for, inside the lines
served.

symbols.name: SourceMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{File string "json:\"file\""; Line int "json:\"line\""; EndLine int "json:\"endLine,omitempty\""; Func string "json:\"func,omitempty\""; GoModule string "json:\"goModule,omitempty\""}
