fields.name: File
fields.doc:
File is relative to App.Root, slash-separated — or, when GoModule is
set, to the root of that Go module.

fields.name: Line
fields.doc: Line is 1-based.

fields.name: EndLine
fields.doc: EndLine, when set, closes the range [Line, EndLine].

fields.name: Func
fields.doc: Func is the qualified Go function, when the range is a function.

fields.name: GoModule
fields.doc:
GoModule is set on a position outside the product's Go module — a
module's (ADR 0008), a library's —: that Go module, "path@version", or
its path alone when it is built from a local directory.

symbols.doc:
SourceMessage locates code.
File is relative to its module's root; Line and EndLine bound the
declaration.

fields.name: TraceID
fields.doc: TraceID groups the spans of one causal chain (W3C, hex).

fields.name: SpanID
fields.doc: SpanID identifies the span (W3C, hex).

fields.name: ParentID
fields.doc: ParentID is the parent span, absent on a root.

fields.name: Node
fields.doc: Node is where the work happened.

fields.name: From
fields.doc: From is the node that caused it: the edge this span travelled.

fields.name: Edge
fields.doc: Edge is the kind of the edge From → Node.

fields.name: Label
fields.doc: Label refines Edge, like the edge's own label.

fields.name: Op
fields.doc: Op is one of the Op constants.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is a low-cardinality operation name: a route pattern, "Get".

fields.name: Start
fields.doc: Start is when the work began.

fields.name: Ms
fields.doc: Ms is how long it took.

fields.name: Status
fields.doc:
Status is StatusError when the product failed — what kit answers with
a 5xx — and StatusOK otherwise, a refusal the caller has to fix (not
found, invalid, conflict, rate limited…) included.

fields.name: Code
fields.doc:
Code is the error code, when the work ended in one: a failure's, or a
refusal's ("not_found").

fields.name: Error
fields.doc: Error is the wire-safe public message of a failure; a refusal has none.

fields.name: Attrs
fields.doc: Attrs are allow-listed attributes: "http.status", "instance"…

fields.name: User
fields.doc: User is the authenticated caller's ID, when there is one.

fields.name: Payload
fields.doc: Payload is what went in and out, in dev only, with secrets redacted.

symbols.doc:
SpanMessage is a finished unit of work, attributed to a node. Only allow-listed,
wire-safe fields travel: no URL, no query string, no private error text.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the state value, as text.

fields.name: Terminal
fields.doc: Terminal is set when no transition leaves the state.

fields.name: Count
fields.doc: Count is how many instances are in the state, on a runtime graph.

fields.name: OnEnter
fields.doc: OnEnter lists the hooks run when an instance enters the state.

symbols.doc:
StateSpec is one state of a workflow.
Terminal marks a state an instance stays in; Count is how many instances
are in it.

symbols.name: StatsMessage

fields.name: Count
fields.doc: Count is how many times it ran.

fields.name: Errors
fields.doc: Errors is how many of those failed.

fields.name: LastAt
fields.doc: LastAt is when it last ran.

fields.name: AvgMs
fields.doc: AvgMs is the mean duration in milliseconds.

fields.name: MaxMs
fields.doc: MaxMs is the longest duration in milliseconds.

symbols.doc:
StatsMessage are observed counters for a node or an edge.
They are counters: they never move a graph's revision.

symbols.name: StatusError
symbols.doc: Span statuses.

symbols.name: StatusOK
symbols.doc: Span statuses.

symbols.name: StepEvent
symbols.spelled: struct{Event string "json:\"event\""; From string "json:\"from\""; To string "json:\"to\""; At time.Time "json:\"at\""; Trigger string "json:\"trigger\""; Caller string "json:\"caller,omitempty\""}

fields.name: Event
fields.doc: Event is the transition's event name.

fields.name: From
fields.doc: From is the state left.

fields.name: To
fields.doc: To is the state entered.

fields.name: At
fields.doc: At is when it happened.

fields.name: Trigger
fields.doc: Trigger is one of the Trigger constants.

fields.name: Caller
fields.doc: Caller is the node that fired it, when code did.

symbols.doc:
StepEvent is one transition in an instance's history.
It carries the event, the states it went from and to, and when it fired.

symbols.name: StoreDataMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{Store string "json:\"store\""; Purpose string "json:\"purpose,omitempty\""; Retention string "json:\"retention,omitempty\""; Recipients []string "json:\"recipients,omitempty\""; Records []json.RawMessage "json:\"records\" kit:\"personal\""; Former []RecordFormerMessage "json:\"former,omitempty\" kit:\"personal\""; Versions []ExportedVersionsMessage "json:\"versions,omitempty\" kit:\"personal\""}

fields.name: Store
fields.doc: Store is the store's node ID.

fields.name: Purpose
fields.doc: Purpose is why the store keeps them.

fields.name: Retention
fields.doc: Retention says, in words, how long they keep their personal data.

fields.name: Recipients
fields.doc:
Recipients are who inside the product reads them, as far as the
running app knows.

fields.name: Records
fields.doc:
Records are the records, their secret members left out. They hold the
person's data, which the Studio and the logs never show.

fields.name: Former
fields.doc:
Former are the former values of the records' fields that keep them
(ADR 0007), record by record; a secret field's are left out.

fields.name: Versions
fields.doc:
Versions are the versions of the records a store with revisions keeps
(ADR 0007 §3), record by record, their secret members left out.

symbols.doc:
StoreDataMessage is one store's records about a person.
It is one part of what kit.Export gives a person about themselves.

symbols.name: StoreErasureMessage

symbols.canonical: struct{Store string "json:\"store\""; Erased []string "json:\"erased,omitempty\" kit:\"personal\""; Deleted []string "json:\"deleted,omitempty\" kit:\"personal\""; Held []string "json:\"held,omitempty\" kit:\"personal\""}

fields.name: Store
fields.doc: Store is the store's node ID.

fields.name: Erased
fields.doc: Erased are the records whose personal data was cleared.

fields.name: Deleted
fields.doc: Deleted are the records removed.

fields.name: Held
fields.doc: Held are the records a hold keeps, untouched.

symbols.doc:
StoreErasureMessage is one store's part of an erasure: the keys of the records
erased, deleted, and held — left in place, as a legal hold asks. A key
may be personal data, which the Studio and the logs never show.

symbols.name: StoreHistoryMessage
symbols.spelled: struct{Revisions int "json:\"revisions,omitempty\""; Fields []string "json:\"fields,omitempty\""; Passwords []PasswordPolicyMessage "json:\"passwords,omitempty\""; Kept *int "json:\"kept,omitempty\""; Bytes *int64 "json:\"bytes,omitempty\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{Revisions int "json:\"revisions,omitempty\""; Fields []string "json:\"fields,omitempty\""; Passwords []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/model/internal/core.PasswordPolicyMessage "json:\"passwords,omitempty\""; Kept *int "json:\"kept,omitempty\""; Bytes *int64 "json:\"bytes,omitempty\""}

fields.name: Revisions
fields.doc:
Revisions is how many former versions each record keeps
(kit.Revisions, ADR 0007 §3); zero when it keeps none.

fields.name: Fields
fields.doc:
Fields are the JSON pointers of the fields that keep their former
values: tagged history=N — the schema's Field.History says how many —
or read by a password policy that refuses former passwords.

fields.name: Passwords
fields.doc: Passwords are the store's password policies.

fields.name: Kept
fields.doc:
Kept is how many former values the store keeps, and Bytes what its
histories weigh, on a runtime graph.

symbols.doc:
StoreHistoryMessage is what a store remembers of its records.
Fields names the fields it keeps former values of; Kept and Bytes weigh
them.

fields.name: Subject
fields.doc:
Subject is the JSON pointer of the field that says whom each record is
about: "/email". Empty when the entity has no subject field.

fields.name: Purpose
fields.doc: Purpose is why the store keeps its records, as kit.Purpose says it.

fields.name: Erase
fields.doc:
Erase says when kit clears a record's personal data; Delete when it
removes the record.

fields.name: ByProduct
fields.doc:
ByProduct is set when the product keeps the store's retention itself
(kit.RetentionByProduct): kit runs none — Erase and Delete are then
absent — and asks for neither a retention nor a subject.

fields.name: HeldUntil
fields.doc:
HeldUntil holds each record until an instant it carries: the law's
own retention (kit.HeldUntil).

fields.name: Anonymise
fields.doc:
Anonymise locates the function that says what an erased record keeps,
generalised (kit.Anonymise).

fields.name: DeleteOnErasure
fields.doc:
DeleteOnErasure: a person's erasure deletes the record instead of
clearing it (kit.DeleteOnErasure).

fields.name: Held
fields.doc: Held is how many records a hold keeps, on a runtime graph.

fields.name: Due
fields.doc:
Due is when the next record is due to be erased or deleted, on a
runtime graph; absent when none is.

fields.name: Erased
fields.doc:
Erased and Deleted count what this run erased and deleted, on a
runtime graph.

symbols.doc:
StorePrivacyMessage is what a store keeps of people: whom each record is about,
why, for how long, and — on a runtime graph — what is held and due.

symbols.name: Version
symbols.doc:
Version is the schema version of every document in this package.

Version 2 adds the auth, mailer and loop kinds, the sends and wakes edges,
the code level of every node ([CodeResult]), the C4 context and containers
([ArchitectureMessage]) and the daemon's own machinery ([RuntimeMessage]).

Version 3 adds the secret kind ([SecretSpec]), the uses edge, the secret
span operation, the rotation loop and the store origin of a setting.

Version 4 is the one bump the decisions of issue #17 share. It adds the
port kind ([PortSpec]) and its binding, a declared edge from the port to
what it calls; the endpoint that implements a port
([EndpointSpec.Implements]), which has no method and no path; and the
replace mock mode ([MockReplace]). ADR 0004 adds the databases: the store's
database ([StoreSpec.Database]), the database container, the database
connector and its adapters, [RuntimeMessage.Databases] and [SettingMessage.Database].
ADR 0008 adds the modules the app mounts ([GraphMessage.Modules]), the module of a
node ([NodeEntity.Module]) and the Go module of a position outside the product's
([SourceMessage.GoModule]); and the watch, a subscription fed by stores: its mark
and the stores that feed it ([SubscriptionSpec.Mark],
[SubscriptionSpec.Stores]), each drawing a declared delivers edge to it.
ADR 0005 adds the command and query kinds ([CommandSpec], [QuerySpec]),
the dispatches and asks edges, the endpoint that exposes one
([EndpointSpec.Exposes]), the read model ([StoreSpec.ReadModel]), the
dispatch, ask and handle span operations and the dispatch and ask
controls.

Version 5 is the first the SDK's framework publishes (ADR 0147). It
adds what a product is made of beyond its services: the binary
([KindBinary]) and its process roles ([KindRole]), the short CLI command
([KindCLI]), the listener that is not HTTP ([KindListener]), the library
shared between components ([KindLibrary]) and the presentation
([KindPresentation]); the edge between two roles of a product, which
carries a versioned contract ([EdgeContracts], [EdgeMessage.Contract]); and the
grammar every ID follows, written once ([IDValue], [ParseID]). It removes what
the Studio no longer does (D13): the respond, fail and delay mock modes,
the control event and its payload — a [MockMessage] is a test's replacement only.

symbols.name: APIBodyTooLarge

code.public: the release metadata is larger than this build accepts

symbols.doc:
APIBodyTooLarge is returned when a release-metadata response exceeds its
read cap.

symbols.name: ArchiveTooLarge

code.public: the release archive is larger than this build accepts

symbols.doc:
ArchiveTooLarge is returned when a release archive exceeds the size cap,
which exists because the bytes are buffered before anything has vouched
for them. It is also what an oversized checksums.txt raises, deliberately
— a truncated manifest fails signature verification, and reporting a size
problem as a supply-chain one is the worst advice this package can give.

symbols.name: ArchiveUnreadable

code.public: the release archive could not be read

symbols.doc:
ArchiveUnreadable is returned when a release archive will not unpack. It
is raised only AFTER the signature and digest have both verified, so it
is a packaging or transfer fault and never a supply-chain signal.

symbols.name: BinaryNotInArchive

code.public: the release archive does not contain the expected binary

symbols.doc:
BinaryNotInArchive is returned when a verified archive does not contain
the expected binary. The archive is authentic; it is a packaging fault
rather than an attack.

symbols.name: Candidate
symbols.doc: Candidate is one release candidate. It aliases the core value type.

symbols.name: CandidateListSentinel
symbols.doc:
CandidateListSentinel is the tag value meaning "list the candidates rather
than install one".

It exists because a CLI flag taking an optional value has to spell "the flag
was given without a value" AS a value. A caller wires it into its own flag
definition, so the sentinel has to be reachable from outside the package that
consumes it.

symbols.name: CandidateNotFound

code.public: no such release candidate

symbols.doc:
CandidateNotFound is returned when a requested release candidate does
not exist.

symbols.name: CandidateTagRequired

code.public: a release candidate is installed by naming its tag, and no tag was named

symbols.doc:
CandidateTagRequired is returned by DownloadCandidate for an empty tag.
It wraps errors.ErrUnsupported, so a caller matching that instead still
matches.

symbols.name: ChecksumMismatch

code.public: the release archive does not match its checksum

symbols.doc:
ChecksumMismatch is returned when the archive's digest does not match
its authenticated manifest entry — a corrupted download, or a release
whose assets changed after it was signed.

symbols.name: ChecksumMissing

code.public: the release has no checksum for this platform

symbols.doc:
ChecksumMissing is returned when the authenticated manifest has no entry
for the archive being installed.

symbols.name: CodeAPIBodyTooLarge
symbols.doc: CodeAPIBodyTooLarge identifies release metadata over its read cap.

symbols.name: CodeArchiveTooLarge
symbols.doc: CodeArchiveTooLarge identifies a release archive over the in-memory cap.

symbols.name: CodeArchiveUnreadable
symbols.doc:
CodeArchiveUnreadable identifies a release archive that would not unpack. It
is raised only AFTER the signature and digest have both verified, so it is a
packaging or transfer fault and never a supply-chain signal.

symbols.name: CodeBinaryNotInArchive
symbols.doc: CodeBinaryNotInArchive identifies a verified archive missing the binary.

symbols.name: CodeCandidateNotFound
symbols.doc: CodeCandidateNotFound identifies a requested candidate that does not exist.

symbols.name: CodeCandidateTagRequired
symbols.doc:
CodeCandidateTagRequired identifies a candidate install asked for without
naming which candidate. It wraps errors.ErrUnsupported, so a caller matching
that instead still matches.

symbols.name: CodeChecksumMismatch
symbols.doc:
CodeChecksumMismatch identifies an archive whose digest did not match its
authenticated manifest entry.

symbols.name: CodeChecksumMissing
symbols.doc:
CodeChecksumMissing identifies an archive with no entry in the authenticated
manifest.

symbols.name: CodeDevBuild
symbols.doc: CodeDevBuild identifies a check on a build with no release version.

symbols.name: CodeDownloadFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeDownloadFailed identifies a download that did not complete. It is the
transient one: a retry is reasonable.

symbols.name: CodeDraftRelease
symbols.doc: CodeDraftRelease identifies a draft release, which exposes no asset.

symbols.name: CodeElevationFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeElevationFailed identifies an escalation the operator DID authorise and
that the system refused anyway. Unlike CodeElevationNotAuthorised, no
environment variable repairs it.

symbols.name: CodeElevationNotAuthorised
symbols.doc:
CodeElevationNotAuthorised identifies a replacement needing privilege the
operator did not opt into. Recoverable, but only through the opt-in.

symbols.name: CodeExecutablePathUnresolved
symbols.doc:
CodeExecutablePathUnresolved identifies an update that cannot name the file
it would replace. Nothing is attempted after it.

symbols.name: CodeInsecureRedirect
symbols.doc: CodeInsecureRedirect identifies a redirect leaving HTTPS or over the hop bound.

symbols.name: CodeInvalidTag
symbols.doc: CodeInvalidTag identifies a tag that is not a valid semantic version.

symbols.name: CodeNoVendorKey
symbols.doc:
CodeNoVendorKey identifies an install attempted by a build carrying no vendor
key. Match it with errs.HasCode: it is the one refusal a retry never fixes.

symbols.name: CodeNotPrerelease
symbols.doc: CodeNotPrerelease identifies a tag requested as a candidate that is stable.

symbols.name: CodeProbeFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeProbeFailed identifies a replacement whose new binary did not answer the
probe the product declared with Service.WithProbe; the previous binary is put
back from <binary>.prev when it was kept (ADR 0150).

symbols.name: CodeReleaseMetadataUnreadable
symbols.doc:
CodeReleaseMetadataUnreadable identifies a release-API answer that arrived
whole and did not decode. The bytes came, so no transport retry applies.

symbols.name: CodeReplacementFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeReplacementFailed identifies a rename over the running executable that did
not land.

symbols.name: CodeSignatureInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeSignatureInvalid identifies a manifest signature that did not verify. With
CodeSignatureMissing it is the supply-chain pair: no retry helps, and no manual
install is safe.

symbols.name: CodeSignatureMissing
symbols.doc: CodeSignatureMissing identifies a release whose manifest signature was absent.

symbols.name: CodeStagingFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeStagingFailed identifies a replacement that failed BEFORE the rename, so
the running binary is byte-for-byte as it was. That is the whole difference
between this and CodeReplacementFailed, and it is the fact an operator needs.

symbols.name: CodeUnexpectedStatus
symbols.doc: CodeUnexpectedStatus identifies an unusable status from the release host.

symbols.name: CodeUnknownArchive
symbols.doc: CodeUnknownArchive identifies an asset in an unhandled container format.

symbols.name: Copier
symbols.doc:
Copier streams the verified archive to its destination. It aliases the core
port.

symbols.name: DevBuild

code.public: this build has no version to compare against a release

symbols.doc:
DevBuild is returned when a version check runs on a build carrying no
release version, so there is nothing to compare a release against. It is
an ANSWER rather than a fault — CheckForUpdate on a `go build` binary
reaches it every time — which is why ExplainUpgradeFailure has no case
for it: "rebuild from source" is NoVendorKey's advice, not this one's.

symbols.name: DownloadFailed

code.public: the release could not be downloaded

symbols.doc:
DownloadFailed is returned when a download does not complete, including
a transport failure with no HTTP status at all. It is the sentinel a
retry policy keys on.

symbols.name: DraftRelease

code.public: that release is still a draft

symbols.doc: DraftRelease is returned for a draft release, which exposes no asset.

symbols.name: ElevationFailed

code.public: the elevated replacement was authorised and the system refused it

symbols.doc:
ElevationFailed is returned when an escalation the operator DID
authorise was refused by the system. Unlike ElevationNotAuthorised, no
environment variable repairs it.

symbols.name: ElevationNotAuthorised

code.public: replacing this binary needs privilege that was not authorised

symbols.doc:
ElevationNotAuthorised is returned when replacing the binary needs
privilege the operator did not opt into. Recoverable — but only through
the opt-in, which ExplainUpgradeFailure names.

symbols.name: ExecutablePathUnresolved

code.public: the path of the running binary could not be resolved, so nothing was replaced

symbols.doc:
ExecutablePathUnresolved is returned when the process cannot work out
which file on disk it runs from. Nothing is attempted after it.

symbols.name: FileSystem
symbols.doc:
FileSystem is the disk half of replacing a running binary. It aliases the core
port.

symbols.name: Getter
symbols.doc: Getter performs the HTTP GETs a self-update needs. It aliases the core port.

symbols.name: InsecureRedirect

code.public: the release host redirected somewhere this build will not follow

symbols.doc:
InsecureRedirect is returned when a redirect leaves HTTPS or exceeds the
hop bound. Following it would hand the archive fetch to a plaintext hop.

symbols.name: InvalidTag

code.public: that is not a valid version tag

symbols.doc: InvalidTag is returned for a tag that is not a valid semantic version.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New returns a Service for the given running version and release source.

The returned Service carries NO vendor key and therefore installs nothing:
chain WithVendorKey with the build's linked-in anchor. That is the safe
direction — a Service that verified only when a key happened to be present
would make the security property depend on a build flag.

symbols.name: NewWithDeps
symbols.spelled: func(version string, src Source, client Getter, fs FileSystem, copier Copier) *Service
symbols.canonical: func(version string, src github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/selfupdate.Source, client github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/selfupdate.Getter, fs github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/selfupdate.FileSystem, copier github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/selfupdate.Copier) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/selfupdate.Service
symbols.doc:
NewWithDeps returns a Service with its three ports injected, for a caller that
supplies its own HTTP policy or a test that supplies doubles. A nil fs or
copier is legal on paths that never reach the disk.

symbols.name: NoVendorKey

code.public: this build cannot verify a release and will not install one

symbols.doc:
NoVendorKey is returned when the running build carries no vendor key,
so nothing could have authenticated the release. A REFUSAL, not a
degradation: there is no weaker check to fall back to.

symbols.name: NotPrerelease

code.public: that tag is a stable release, not a candidate

symbols.doc:
NotPrerelease is returned when a tag requested as a candidate is
reported as a stable release.

symbols.name: ProbeFailed

code.public: the new binary did not answer its probe and was not kept

symbols.doc:
ProbeFailed is returned when the replaced binary did not answer its
probe; rolled_back says whether <binary>.prev was put back.

symbols.name: ReleaseMetadataUnreadable

code.public: the release host's answer could not be read as release metadata

symbols.doc:
ReleaseMetadataUnreadable is returned when the release API answers
within its cap and the body does not decode. The bytes arrived, so no
transport retry applies.

symbols.name: ReplacementFailed

code.public: the running binary could not be replaced

symbols.doc:
ReplacementFailed is returned when the rename over the running
executable did not land.

symbols.name: Service
symbols.doc:
Service replaces the running binary with a newer signed release. It aliases
the service type — the engine handle, per ADR 0074.

symbols.name: SignatureInvalid

code.public: the release signature did not verify

symbols.doc:
SignatureInvalid is returned when the manifest's signature does not
verify against the vendor key. With SignatureMissing it is the
supply-chain pair: no retry helps and no manual install is safe.

symbols.name: SignatureMissing

code.public: the release is not signed

symbols.doc:
SignatureMissing is returned when the detached signature over the
checksum manifest could not be fetched. An unsigned release is never
installed and no environment variable reopens that.

symbols.name: Source
symbols.doc:
Source says where releases come from and what they are called. It aliases the
service type: these are one engine's construction parameters, which ADR 0074
places with the engine rather than in the contract layer.

symbols.name: StagingFailed

code.public: the update could not be staged, and the running binary was left untouched

symbols.doc:
StagingFailed is returned when the replacement failed BEFORE the rename,
so the running binary is byte-for-byte as it was. That is the whole
difference between this and ReplacementFailed.

symbols.name: StdinIsTerminal
symbols.doc:
StdinIsTerminal reports whether a human could answer a prompt on this
process's standard input.

It is a free function rather than something AuthoriseUnattendedUpgrade works
out for itself, and that is the point: the consent decision stays testable
without a pty, because the CALLER supplies the answer. Pass the result as the
interactive argument.

symbols.name: UnexpectedStatus

code.public: the release host answered unexpectedly

symbols.doc:
UnexpectedStatus is returned when the release host answers with a status
the update path does not accept. Retryable.

symbols.name: UnknownArchive

code.public: the release archive format is not supported

symbols.doc:
UnknownArchive is returned for an asset whose container format is not
handled.

symbols.name: Update
symbols.doc:
Update is the outcome of a version check or an install. It aliases the core
value type.

symbols.name: CodeMisconfigured
symbols.doc:
CodeMisconfigured identifies an exporter configuration that cannot be
honoured: no socket path, a buffer outside its bounds, an ID outside the
grammar in the node table.

symbols.name: CodeRunning
symbols.doc: CodeRunning identifies a Start on an exporter already started.

symbols.name: Decode
symbols.spelled: func(b []byte) (e Event, seq uint64, ok bool)
symbols.doc:
Decode reads one record, as a client does: the event and its sequence
number. ok is false for a record of another size or version.

symbols.name: DefaultBuffer
symbols.doc: The ring's bounds and default, in events.

symbols.name: Emitter
symbols.doc:
Emitter is where a product reports: the telemetry port. Emit copies e and
never keeps it; it must not block and must not allocate.

symbols.name: Event
symbols.spelled: struct{Kind Kind; Op Op; Outcome Outcome; Node NodeRef; From NodeRef; Code uint32; Start int64; Duration int64; TraceID [16]byte; SpanID [8]byte}
symbols.canonical: struct{Kind github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/telemetry.Kind; Op github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/telemetry.Op; Outcome github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/telemetry.Outcome; Node github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/telemetry.NodeRef; From github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/telemetry.NodeRef; Code uint32; Start int64; Duration int64; TraceID [16]byte; SpanID [8]byte}

fields.name: Node
fields.doc: Node is where the work ran; From, the node it came from, if any.

fields.name: From
fields.doc: Node is where the work ran; From, the node it came from, if any.

fields.name: Code
fields.doc: Code is the dotted-quad code of the error that ended it, 0 for none.

fields.name: Start
fields.doc: Start is when it began, in Unix nanoseconds; Duration, how long it took.

fields.name: Duration
fields.doc: Start is when it began, in Unix nanoseconds; Duration, how long it took.

fields.name: TraceID
fields.doc: TraceID and SpanID are the trace's, when there is one.

symbols.doc:
Event is one report. Its fields are numbers only — see the package comment:
there is no field a person's data could travel in, in any environment.

symbols.name: Exporter
symbols.doc:
Exporter is an Emitter that hands events to the clients attached to its
socket. It never blocks a producer: a full ring drops the event and counts
it.

symbols.name: Dropped
symbols.doc: Dropped is how many events a full ring refused.

symbols.name: Emit
symbols.doc:
Emit copies ev into the ring, or drops it when the ring is full. It never
blocks and never allocates.

symbols.name: Instance
symbols.doc: Instance is the process's instance identifier, in the handshake.

symbols.name: Ref
symbols.doc:
Ref is the reference of node id in the handshake's table; zero when the
table does not hold it.

symbols.name: Sent
symbols.doc: Sent is how many records reached at least one client.

symbols.name: Start
symbols.doc:
Start opens the socket and starts the two goroutines: one accepts clients
and greets them, one drains the ring to them. Both end at Stop.

symbols.name: Stop
symbols.doc: Stop closes the socket and every client, and waits for the goroutines.

symbols.name: ExporterConfig
symbols.spelled: struct{Path string; AllowUIDs []int; AllowGIDs []int; Buffer int; Hello HelloValue}
symbols.canonical: struct{Path string; AllowUIDs []int; AllowGIDs []int; Buffer int; Hello github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/telemetry.HelloValue}

fields.name: Path
fields.doc: Path is the private socket's absolute path (pkg/v1/proc/ipc).

fields.name: AllowUIDs
fields.doc:
AllowUIDs and AllowGIDs admit accounts besides the product's own: the
on-call group declared at deployment.

fields.name: AllowGIDs
fields.doc:
AllowUIDs and AllowGIDs admit accounts besides the product's own: the
on-call group declared at deployment.

fields.name: Buffer
fields.doc:
Buffer is the ring's size in events, rounded up to a power of two, in
[MinBuffer, MaxBuffer]; zero is DefaultBuffer.

fields.name: Hello
fields.doc: Hello is what the handshake says.

symbols.doc:
ExporterConfig is where the exporter listens, who may attach, and how much
it holds for a slow reader.

symbols.name: HelloValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Product string; Binary string; Role string; Revision string; Digest string; Nodes []string}
symbols.canonical: struct{Product string; Binary string; Role string; Revision string; Digest string; Nodes []string}

fields.name: Product
fields.doc:
Product, Binary and Role name what runs: the app, the binary and the
process role it is (framework/model's IDs).

fields.name: Binary
fields.doc:
Product, Binary and Role name what runs: the app, the binary and the
process role it is (framework/model's IDs).

fields.name: Role
fields.doc:
Product, Binary and Role name what runs: the app, the binary and the
process role it is (framework/model's IDs).

fields.name: Revision
fields.doc: Revision is the VCS commit the binary was built from (vcs.revision).

fields.name: Digest
fields.doc: Digest is the design's digest the code was generated from, when known.

fields.name: Nodes
fields.doc: Nodes are the node IDs events refer to: Nodes[i] is NodeRef(i+1).

symbols.doc:
HelloValue is what the handshake says about the process, besides the
operations and the record size: which product, binary and role run, from
which revision and design, and the node table events refer to.

symbols.name: Kind
symbols.doc: Kind says what an event reports.

symbols.name: KindPhase
symbols.doc:
KindPhase is the process changing phase: starting, serving, draining,
stopped, failed — Op carries it.

symbols.name: KindSpan
symbols.doc: KindSpan is one unit of work that ended on a node.

symbols.name: MaxBuffer
symbols.doc: The ring's bounds and default, in events.

symbols.name: MinBuffer
symbols.doc: The ring's bounds and default, in events.

symbols.name: Misconfigured

code.public: The telemetry exporter is misconfigured

symbols.doc:
Misconfigured refuses an exporter that cannot be built as asked; the
rule field says which rule failed.

symbols.name: NewExporter
symbols.doc:
NewExporter checks cfg and builds an exporter that listens nowhere yet:
Start opens its socket.

symbols.name: NodeRef
symbols.doc:
NodeRef is a node's index in the handshake's node table, from 1; zero is
"no node".

symbols.name: Nop
symbols.doc:
Nop is the emitter that reports nothing: what a product holds unless it
was started with an exporter.

symbols.name: Op
symbols.doc: Op is what the work was: the span operations of framework/model.
